articles.title: 'Dealing with you was horrendous': Former NSW coach Anthony Stuart hits back at Usman Khawaja amid Sandpapergate controversy
articles.summary: Former New South Wales coach Anthony Stuart has responded strongly to criticism from retired Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his autobiography.
articles.body: Former New South Wales coach Anthony Stuart has responded strongly to criticism from retired Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his autobiography. Stuart took to social media to share his side of the story and recalled several incidents from Khawaja's time with the NSW team.Khawaja had written about his experience under Stuart before moving to Queensland to play Sheffield Shield cricket in 2012. He questioned the support he received from his former coach and said he could not build a good relationship with him.“Anthony Stuart was a good enough guy but as a coach he didn’t do anything for me,” Khawaja wrote.“I tried so hard to build a rapport, talk to him about himself or his family and I just got nothing," he wrote.Stuart, who played three one-day internationals for Australia, said he had already shared his views about Khawaja privately with friends. He also responded to the batter's comments about their relationship.Stuart said he did not remember Khawaja asking him about his family or personal life. He also apologised if his response had not been what the batter expected.“My memory is pretty good, but apparently I didn’t disclose that, or anything else about my private life, to you. I certainly don’t remember you ever asking about my family, but if we did, I apologise for not engaging to your liking," Stuart wrote.Stuart recalls issues during trainingThe former NSW coach also spoke about what he described as Khawaja's “regular complaining” during his playing days. He pointed to an incident during training when the batter continued to wear his pads after finishing his batting session.“Constantly walking around training with your pads on after batting,” he wrote.“Pretty hard to then bowl to the teammates that had just spent time bowling to you. “Or was it just a coincidence?"Dispute over batting positionStuart also recalled a disagreement over Khawaja's batting position in a Sheffield Shield match in Tasmania. He claimed Khawaja and his manager had strongly objected to him opening the batting for NSW.The team at the time included established batters such as Steve Smith, Simon Katich and Phil Hughes. Stuart said Smith was the team's best batter and should bat at No. 3. Smith went on to score 98 in that match.“You, and then your manager at the time, having a massive tantrum about you having to open the batting for NSW in a shield game in Tasmania, when the best player ‘should bat three’," he said.“Hate to break it to you, but they were all better players than you. Your manager was right, our best player should bat three. He (Smith) did. He got 98. Dealing with you, and your manager back then, and again I paraphrase you, was just horrendous,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'He's breaking the door down': Former cricketer's big praise for Priyansh Arya after record-breaking 181 in SMAT
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India domestic cricket stalwart Priyank Panchal has thrown his weight behind Priyansh Arya's potential India call-up after the young
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India domestic cricket stalwart Priyank Panchal has thrown his weight behind Priyansh Arya's potential India call-up after the young Delhi and Punjab Kings batter produced a record-breaking knock in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT), saying he is "breaking the door down" with his performances.Arya smashed a sensational 181 off just 68 balls against Tamil Nadu on Tuesday, becoming the highest-scoring Indian batter in T20 cricket history. His innings, featuring seven fours and 19 sixes at a strike rate of 266, helped Delhi post a massive 275/5 in 20 overs.The 25-year-old surpassed KL Rahul's previous Indian record of 152 not out off 67 balls, scored for Delhi Capitals against Punjab Kings at the Arun Jaitley Stadium earlier this year. Rahul's knock was also the first 150-plus individual score by an Indian in IPL history.Taking to X, Panchal praised Arya's progress across formats and pointed to his performances in the IPL, domestic cricket and India A assignments as evidence of his growing credentials."Priyansh Arya has been in sensational form in the IPL. And he has been rewarded for that with India A appearances too. Now, with such SMAT performances, where he’s scoring 180+ runs, he’s breaking the door down. Don’t forget he got a fine century in Ranji Trophy too this season!" Panchal wrote.IPL impact, Ranji Trophy returns strengthen Arya's caseArya has been among the most exciting young batters in Indian cricket. In the 2026 IPL season, he scored 364 runs in 13 innings for PBKS at an average of 28 and a strike rate of 211.62, including three half-centuries.He had announced himself during PBKS' 2025 runners-up campaign, finishing with 475 runs in 17 innings at a strike rate of nearly 180, including a century and two fifties.His red-ball numbers have also been impressive. In three Ranji Trophy appearances for Delhi this season, Arya has scored 311 runs across four innings at an average of 77.75, including a century and a half-century. His highest score was 199 against Gujarat.Arya has also featured regularly for India A. He scored 101 off 84 balls against Australia A on his debut in October 2025 and made 137 runs in four innings during the 50-over tri-series in June. More recently, he scored 49 off 45 balls against Australia A in October.Arya enters record books with stunning SMAT assaultThe latest innings has placed Arya among the biggest individual performers in T20 history. His 181 is the second-highest individual score in the format, behind South Africa's Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who made 188 off 79 balls for Titans against Knights in the CSA Pro20 Cup in October.Arya also equalled Finn Allen's world record of 19 sixes in a single T20 innings. His score is the highest in SMAT history, surpassing Tilak Varma's 151 for Hyderabad against Meghalaya in November 2024.Delhi's 275/5 was the third-highest total in the tournament's history. Tamil Nadu, in reply, were bowled out for 159 in 18.3 overs, with Digvesh Rathi taking four wickets, Suyash Sharma claiming three and Mayank Yadav picking up two.Arya is also leading the run charts this SMAT season, with 362 runs in six innings at an average of 60.33 and a strike rate of 204.51, including a century and three half-centuries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Had a feeling I would score a hundred':  India-born Harpreet Bhatia's emotional ton on Guru Nanak Jayanti against India A
articles.summary: An India-born cricketer who once represented the country at the U-19 level and featured in the IPL turned the spotlight on himself with a memorable
articles.body: An India-born cricketer who once represented the country at the U-19 level and featured in the IPL turned the spotlight on himself with a memorable century against India A in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday.Harpreet Singh Bhatia, who represented Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh in Indian domestic cricket before becoming a UAE citizen earlier this year, produced a remarkable 130 off 144 deliveries to guide the UAE to 249/8 in their Group B encounter.The 35-year-old, who has also featured in nine IPL matches for franchises including Punjab Kings, Kolkata Knight Riders and Rising Pune Supergiants, held the UAE innings together after the team lost its opening wickets cheaply. His knock featured 12 boundaries and four sixes, as he registered his seventh List A century and surpassed his previous best score of 121.Harpreet Singh Recalls Emotional Century Against IndiaHaving spent a significant part of his cricketing career in India, Harpreet's century against India A carried special significance. The left-hander admitted that scoring runs against a quality opposition like India was a major motivation."There was always motivation to score against a big team. And India is a very good side, and I'm glad that I made it," Harpreet said.He also revealed that he had a special feeling about scoring a century on the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti."And I had a thought this morning that today is Guru Nanak Jayanti. I got a feeling that I'm going to score a hundred today. So it has come after a very long time on Guru Nanak Jayanti. I want to wish everyone a happy Gurpurab," he added.The former India U-19 player looked comfortable against the India A bowling attack and particularly enjoyed taking on pacer Harshit Rana, whom he struck for a couple of sixes down the ground. One of those maximums came off a slower delivery and also brought up his seventh List A hundred.Arshad Khan Ends Harpreet's Resistance, India A Restrict UAE To 249Harpreet continued to anchor the UAE innings as wickets kept falling at the other end. However, his impressive knock eventually came to an end in the 47th over when left-arm pacer Arshad Khan bowled him for 130 off 144 deliveries.Arshad was the standout performer for India A, finishing with figures of 4/43 in his 10 overs. Harshit Rana, meanwhile, endured an expensive outing, conceding 63 runs in his 10 overs while picking up one wicket. The pacer is also looking to prove his match fitness after returning from injury.Despite Harpreet's century, the other UAE batters struggled to maintain momentum and failed to convert their starts into substantial contributions, allowing India A to restrict them to 249/8 in 50 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ends 12-year wait, smashes 100 off 28 balls to surpass Suresh Raina's famous 87 off 25
articles.summary: Suresh Raina's breathtaking 87 off 25 balls for Chennai Super Kings against Kings XI Punjab in IPL 2014 had remained one of the most iconic power-hitting
articles.body: Suresh Raina's breathtaking 87 off 25 balls for Chennai Super Kings against Kings XI Punjab in IPL 2014 had remained one of the most iconic power-hitting displays in Indian cricket. More than a decade later, teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has produced an innings that has taken the comparison to another level, smashing a sensational 100 off just 28 deliveries for India A against the UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday.Raina's extraordinary knock came during the IPL 2014 Qualifier 2 at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on May 30. Chasing a daunting 227-run target, the left-hander went berserk, smashing 12 fours and six sixes at a staggering strike rate of 348. He scored 87 runs in just 25 balls before being run out on the first delivery of the seventh over.His 87-run effort remains the highest individual score inside the six-over powerplay in IPL history. However, Sooryavanshi has now surpassed that tally in a remarkable display of power-hitting, reaching his century in just 28 balls against UAE.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 28-ball carnage against UAEOpening the innings for India A in a 250-run chase, Sooryavanshi launched an astonishing assault on the UAE bowling attack from the very first over.The 15-year-old brought up his half-century in just 16 deliveries, smashing eight sixes in the process. He showed no signs of slowing down and continued to clear the boundary with remarkable ease.Sooryavanshi eventually reached the three-figure mark in just 28 balls, becoming the fastest centurion in List A cricket history. His innings featured 13 sixes and four boundaries, as he dismantled the UAE bowling attack inside the first seven overs. The youngster completed his century by smashing Ibrar Ahmad for a boundary in the seventh over, sparking celebrations in the India A dressing room.Raina's 87 off 25 remains one of the most memorable knocks in IPL history, particularly because of the circumstances in which it came. Chennai Super Kings were chasing 227 against Kings XI Punjab in the second qualifier of IPL 2014. After losing Faf du Plessis early, Raina walked in and immediately took the attack to the opposition.He smashed 12 fours and six sixes, scoring at a strike rate of 348. His extraordinary assault included a 33-run over against Parvinder Awana, which briefly brought CSK back into contention.However, Raina was run out for 87 on the first ball of the seventh over, ending a remarkable innings. CSK eventually finished at 202/7, losing the contest by 24 runs. More than 12 years later, Sooryavanshi has delivered another extraordinary batting spectacle, surpassing Raina's famous 87-run tally in a completely different format and setting.India A's must-win clash Against UAEIndia A entered the contest under pressure after losing their previous Group B encounter against Pakistan Shaheens. The side needed a strong response to keep its qualification hopes alive. Earlier, Harpreet Singh Bhatia had anchored the UAE innings with an impressive 130 off 144 balls, helping his side post 249/8 in 50 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India A complete record-breaking chase, hammer UAE by seven wickets in just 14.2 overs after Sooryavanshi's 204
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages, smashing a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls as India A chased down 250 against the United Arab
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages, smashing a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls as India A chased down 250 against the United Arab Emirates in just 14.2 overs to register a seven-wicket victory in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday.Harpreet Singh Bhatia's Century Rescues UAE After Early CollapseUAE skipper Basil Hameed won the toss and opted to bat first, but the decision did not immediately pay dividends as India A struck early with the ball. Harshit Rana removed opener Aryansh Sharma for two, while Arshad Khan dismissed Ansh Tandon for eight to leave UAE struggling at 20/2 inside the first six overs.With the innings in danger of falling apart, Harpreet Singh Bhatia took responsibility and anchored the recovery. The former India U-19 cricketer, who has also featured in the IPL, showed tremendous composure against the India A bowling attack. Harpreet stitched together a crucial 71-run partnership with Muhammad Shahdad, who contributed 28 off 46 deliveries. The left-hander then continued to hold one end together as Ethan D'Souza added 25 off 37 balls.Harpreet eventually brought up a memorable century and continued batting deep into the innings. His 130 off 144 deliveries featured 12 fours and four sixes, making it a career-best List A score. However, Arshad Khan ended his resistance in the 47th over, bowling him for 130. Arshad continued his impressive spell by dismissing Ibrar Ahmad for a duck in the following over.Captain Basil Hameed provided some late resistance with an unbeaten 36 off 36 balls, helping UAE finish at 249/8 in 50 overs.Arshad was the standout bowler for India A, finishing with figures of 4/43 in 10 overs. Harshit Rana conceded 63 runs but picked up one wicket, while Harsh Dubey, Shahbaz Ahmed and Suryansh Shedge also claimed a wicket each.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi goes berserkChasing 250, India A could not have asked for a more explosive start from their opening pair of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma. Sooryavanshi attacked from the very first over, taking on UAE pacer Zahid Ali with three consecutive sixes in the opening over. He continued his assault against Ibrar Ahmad and Basil Hameed, reaching his half-century in just 16 deliveries.Abhishek Sharma joined the six-hitting spree, but his stay was brief as he was dismissed by Ibrar Ahmad for 12 off five balls. Sooryavanshi, however, continued to dominate the UAE attack and brought up his century in just 28 deliveries. The teenager broke Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk's previous record of a 29-ball List A century, creating history with his extraordinary knock.Prabhsimran Singh also failed to make a significant contribution, departing for three off four balls, but the wickets did little to slow Sooryavanshi down. The left-hander continued his assault and reached 150 in just 40 balls, making it one of the most extraordinary power-hitting displays in the history of List A cricket.Sooryavanshi's assault reached another level as he continued to clear the boundary with remarkable ease. He brought up his double century in just 53 deliveries, becoming the fastest batter to score 200 in List A cricket. His final tally of 28 sixes broke the previous record of 26 maximums in a professional cricket innings, held by Hyderabad's Tanmay Agarwal.Sooryavanshi eventually departed for 204 off 53 balls after attempting to clear long-off against Basil Hameed in the 13th over. Aryansh Sharma completed the catch as the UAE captain finally ended the teenage sensation's monumental innings.Rinku Singh finishes the chase as India A seal dominant victoryWith the target almost within reach, Rinku Singh ensured there were no further twists in the contest. He remained unbeaten on 21 off 17 deliveries, while Kumar Kushagra was unbeaten on one. Rinku brought the chase to a close in the 15th over, smashing Basil Hameed for a six over deep mid-wicket as India A reached 254/3 in just 14.2 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I do feel pressure': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opens up after record-breaking double century
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have rewritten the List A record books with a breathtaking 53-ball double century, but the teenager revealed that there was no
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have rewritten the List A record books with a breathtaking 53-ball double century, but the teenager revealed that there was no change in his mindset going into the record-breaking innings against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday.The 15-year-old smashed an astonishing 204 off just 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes, the most ever by a batter in List A cricket, as India A chased down UAE's 250-run target in just 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets in their Group B encounter in Doha.Sooryavanshi registered the fastest century and double century in List A cricket, reaching the 100-run milestone in just 28 balls before completing his double hundred off 52 deliveries. He also became the first batter to score two List A half-centuries in 16 balls or fewer.Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Sooryavanshi explained that his approach was initially to spend time at the crease after failing to convert his starts in the previous two matches. However, he quickly realised that the surface offered little assistance to the bowlers and decided to back his natural attacking game."In the last two matches, I got set but couldn't convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren't getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths," Sooryavanshi said.The left-hander revealed that his focus was simply on assessing the conditions and adjusting his approach accordingly, rather than thinking about records or milestones."There wasn't anything specific on my mind. The only thought was that if the wicket was helping the bowlers, I would take my time and play a longer innings. But thankfully, that wasn't the case. The wicket was good, the ball was coming nicely onto the bat, so I tried to back my game," he added.'Same mindset of trying to bat deep'Despite producing one of the most extraordinary innings in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi insisted that his mindset remained unchanged. He said his priority was always to bat deep and take control of the game once he settled in."Nothing different, sir. It was the same mindset of trying to bat deep. If the game wasn't in my control initially, I would look to take my time. But thankfully, I was able to take control early on, and then I played the game on my terms," he said.Sooryavanshi also spoke about his experience of captaining Bihar, describing it as an enjoyable responsibility. He credited the senior players around him for making the environment comfortable and encouraging open discussions within the team."It was a lot of fun captaining Bihar, and the team is doing quite well too. Hopefully, Bihar continue performing the same way. As far as this team is concerned, I've been around all the senior players for a long time, so I'm very comfortable with them. They make me feel at ease, everyone speaks openly, and whenever they have a suggestion, they share it with me. I listen to everyone," he said.'If I just watch the ball properly, the game will be easy'The teenage batter also revealed the consistent advice he receives from his coaches, particularly Hrishi sir, who has been guiding him since his Under-19 days."Hrishi sir, for example, keeps telling me the same thing before every match. He has been saying this since Under-19. He tells me that if I just watch the ball properly, the game will be easy for me," Sooryavanshi said.Having rediscovered his rhythm against UAE, the youngster is now hoping to carry the momentum into the remaining matches of the tournament."It feels good. I've got my flow back in the game, so I'll try to carry this forward into the remaining matches of the tournament. Hopefully, we win the semi final and reach the final, and I can continue playing with the same flow and in my own way," he added.Interestingly, despite his fearless approach and record-breaking hitting, Sooryavanshi admitted that he does feel pressure while batting. However, he said the nerves usually settle after facing a few deliveries."Absolutely, You do feel a little pressure. It's normal, it's human nature to feel a bit nervous. But after two or four balls, I settle down and get back to normal," he said.India A entered the UAE contest under pressure after losing to Pakistan Shaheens in their previous match and needing a win to strengthen their semi-final qualification hopes. Sooryavanshi's extraordinary innings ensured a dominant response, with the youngster producing a performance that will be remembered for its remarkable collection of records.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Chhattisgarh-born Harpreet Singh Bhatia scored a century for UAE after rising through MP cricket, later captaining Chhattisgarh and moving to UAE in 2026.
articles.body: Raipur: Chhattisgarh-born batter Harpreet Singh Bhatia scored a century for the UAE on Tuesday, completing a remarkable journey that began in Madhya Pradesh because his home state had no place in Indian cricket’s national structure at the time.Chhattisgarh was a newly formed state in 2000 and had no permanent BCCI membership then. Bhatia, born in Chhattisgarh’s Dallirajhara, moved up through MP’s Under-14, Under-17, Under-19 and Under-23 squads before making his Ranji Trophy debut for them.When Chhattisgarh finally received full BCCI membership in 2016, he went home. He played Ranji Trophy cricket for Chhattisgarh from 2018 to 2024 and captained the side for three consecutive years before the Covid-19 pandemic. He then returned to Madhya Pradesh, where he played until 2026. In the IPL, he played for Kolkata Knight Riders, Pune Warriors India and Punjab Kings.Despite consistent, standout performances in domestic cricket, the 35-year-old saw limited prospects of breaking into the Indian national team. Seeking new opportunities, he moved to the UAE in January 2026, while his wife remained in Dallirajhara, according to his father, garment trader Jashpal Singh Bhatia (65).Bhatia settled in quickly. He began playing in the UAE in February 2026, securing a spot in the national ODI team. articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's sensational 204 off just 53 balls powered India A to a historic seven-wicket victory over the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's sensational 204 off just 53 balls powered India A to a historic seven-wicket victory over the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha on Tuesday. The teenager's extraordinary batting display helped India A chase down a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs, setting multiple team records in the process.Quickest chase of 200-plus targetIndia A's successful chase of 250 in 14.2 overs is the quickest instance of a team chasing down a target of 200 or more in List A cricket. The previous record belonged to Allied Bank Limited, who had completed a 200-plus chase in 20 overs against Service Industries in Lahore during the 2003 Patron's Cup. India A bettered that mark by almost six overs, producing a remarkable batting display to seal the contest.The team also registered the quickest 100 in List A cricket, reaching the milestone in just five overs. New Zealand previously held the record after scoring 100 in 6.3 overs against Sri Lanka in Christchurch in 2015. India A also went past their own effort of 6.3 overs against Sri Lanka A in Dambulla in 2026, while New Zealand's 6.4-over effort against England in Wellington in 2015 features among the fastest team hundreds.Quickest team 100 in List A one day cricket5 overs India A vs UAE Doha 20266.3 NZ vs SL Christchurch 20156.3 India A vs SL A Dambulla 20266.4 NZ vs England Wellington 2015India A's six-hitting display was equally remarkable, with the team smashing 31 maximums during the chase. It is the second-highest number of sixes hit by a team in a List A innings, behind Bihar's record of 38 against Arunachal Pradesh in Ranchi in 2025. Sooryavanshi accounted for 28 of India's sixes.Sooryavanshi's 204 headlines India's record-breaking chaseSooryavanshi smashed 204 off just 53 deliveries, with his innings featuring seven fours and 28 sixes. He brought up his century in just 28 balls before completing his double hundred in 53 deliveries, adding another landmark performance to his growing list of records.Earlier, UAE had posted 249/8 in their 50 overs, with Harpreet Singh Bhatia leading the innings with a brilliant 130 off 144 balls. articles.title: From fastest double century to most sixes: List of records Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shattered with his 204 against UAE
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages as he rewrote the record books with a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the ACC
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced an innings for the ages as he rewrote the record books with a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday. The 15-year-old India A opener smashed 28 sixes and seven fours, registering one of the most extraordinary batting performances in professional cricket.Sooryavanshi's incredible knock helped India A chase down a target of 250 in just 14.2 overs, securing a seven-wicket victory. In the process, the youngster broke multiple records across List A and professional cricket, setting new benchmarks for batting strike rates, fastest centuries, double centuries and six-hitting.Here is a look at the records Sooryavanshi created with his sensational innings.1. Highest strike rate in a List A centurySooryavanshi registered a staggering strike rate of 384.90, the highest ever in a List A innings featuring a century. He surpassed former South Africa captain AB de Villiers, who had held the record for over a decade after scoring 149 off 44 balls at a strike rate of 338.63 against the West Indies in Johannesburg in 2015.Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk occupies the third position with his 125 off 38 balls at a strike rate of 328.94 for South Australia against Tasmania in 2023.2. Fastest double century in List A cricketThe India A opener smashed the fastest double century in List A cricket, reaching the 200-run mark in just 52 balls. He comfortably surpassed the previous record held by Chad Bowes, who had taken 103 deliveries to score a double century for Canterbury against Otago in Christchurch in 2024.Tamil Nadu's N Jagadeesan and England's Harry Brook are next on the list, having reached their respective double centuries in 114 balls.3. Most sixes in an innings in professional cricketSooryavanshi smashed an astonishing 28 sixes, setting a new record for the most maximums hit in a single innings across professional cricket. He went past Tanmay Agarwal's previous record of 26 sixes, scored for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in a Ranji Trophy match in 2024.Colin Munro and D'Arcy Short had previously struck 23 sixes each in their respective innings.4. Most sixes in a List A inningsThe teenager also set a new record for the most sixes in a single List A innings with his 28 maximums against the UAE. Australia's D'Arcy Short previously held the record with 23 sixes for Western Australia against Queensland in 2018.Bevon Jacobs is third on the list with 21 sixes for Auckland against Otago in 2026.5. His previous best was a 32-ball hundred for India A against the UAE in a T20 match in 2025.He has also scored centuries off 35 balls for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans in 2025 and 36 balls for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in List A cricket in 2025, as well as for Rajasthan Royals against Sunrisers Hyderabad in 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India's Christchurch dilemma: Does Gurnoor Brar get the nod?
articles.summary: CHRISTCHURCH: With just a three-day turnaround between the two Tests, India cancelled their practice session on November 25.
articles.body: CHRISTCHURCH: With just a three-day turnaround between the two Tests, India cancelled their practice session on November 25. Collectively, the fast bowlers sent down 182 overs in the series opener, so balancing the need to keep their bodies fresh is hardly surprising. Shubman Gill & Co. are set to train on the eve of the match and will hold another selection huddle ahead of the second Test, starting Friday.Tuesday was a rather unusual day, even for the locals, which kept the city centre buzzing. The Indian cricketers didn't waste a moment after checking into their city hotel, heading out in different groups to grab a quick bite near the team hotel. The sun was out and the breeze was gentle enough to keep the caps in place. The locals, however, had a word of caution, suggesting a wild week ahead."You never know with Christchurch. It is not as windy as Wellington, but the forecast can surprise you. It can be a bit wild, so keep checking the app," says a staff member at a popular Indian restaurant. "Do keep the umbrellas handy," she adds with a chuckle.Although rain is forecast on some days, conditions currently look largely pleasant, with temperatures hovering in the 20s. Unlike Wellington, there are no wild spells of wind here. Most of India's Test players are very well accustomed to this city, having spent a lot of time here when the A team played three fixtures preceding the Tests.From Jasprit Bumrah to Yashasvi Jaiswal, as many as 13 squad members have had game time here, and seven of them played the second A game at Hagley Oval. It was a high-scoring fixture where Jaiswal and Dhruv Jurel scored tons, and it followed a pattern similar to Wellington: early wickets followed by a struggle once the ball got old.The scenario is likely to be discussed when the captain and coach firm up their plans for the second game. Even though Gill lauded the current group for their energy and body language on a flat pitch, Gurnoor Brar will be back in the discussion for his extra pace and ability to bowl long spells without losing pace.The fast bowler from Punjab was very close to making his debut in Colombo, but the think tank persisted with the experience of Siraj. The move backfired, and it will be interesting to see whether they are adventurous enough to tweak the quartet of Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj. It could sound like a harsh call or a knee-jerk reaction, but India need to assemble an attack capable of making inroads even when there is nothing on offer. And that could well be the case in Christchurch too.No matter how much grass the curator leaves on the pitch, if the conditions overhead are not supportive, a Basin-like blockathon could well return to the menu. Prasidh was very underwhelming in the first innings of the first Test but found his rhythm in the second and looked the most effective bowler. Akash set up the game nicely in the first innings, and Kamboj did his job with both bat and ball.So who goes out if Brar comes in? A tricky call awaits the management as they chase crucial World Test Championship points. A draw won't suffice for a team pressing for a final berth, and an unfavourable result this week could well draw curtains on their slim hopes. For a side emphasising current form over reputation, it will be interesting to see how the selection plays out over the next couple of days.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Selector must have stature, not just a seat at the table: Dilip Vengsarkar
articles.summary: At a time when India’s team selection has come under scrutiny following the controversial calls involving Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja in
articles.body: At a time when India’s team selection has come under scrutiny following the controversial calls involving Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja in Wellington, former India captain and chief selector Dilip Vengsarkar believes the solution lies not merely in having a selector travel with the team, but in ensuring that the men doing the job have the stature to challenge the captain and coach.Vengsarkar, widely regarded as one of India’s finest chairmen of selectors, feels the travelling selector cannot simply be an observer. He should be part of the process of choosing the playing XI and, crucially, be strong enough to intervene when he believes the team management is getting a major call wrong.“When I was chairman of the selection committee, if any member of the five-man committee went on a tour, he would chair the selection meeting along with the captain and vice-captain. The meeting would be convened by the manager,” Vengsarkar told TOI.“So, automatically, the selector chairing the meeting had a say in the playing XI. The meeting should involve the selector, coach, captain and vice-captain and be convened by the manager,” he stated.With Shubman Gill still inexperienced in his job as Test captain, should the selection committee then carry greater responsibility over what XI plays?Vengsarkar believes the captain’s age or experience is not necessarily the issue here.“It depends on the stature of the person who is the selector there on tour. If a person without stature accompanies the team, he can be influenced or dominated,” he said.During Vengsarkar’s stint as chief selector, his panel included Venkatapathy Raju, Ranjib Biswal, Bhupinder Singh Sr and Sanjay Jagdale. Vengsarkar says he and Jagdale chaired selection meetings when they travelled with the team.He recalled an episode from a tour which, without naming the captain or coach involved, illustrated why a strong selector could become an important balancing presence.“The coach told me to sort things out because he felt slighted as the captain was not consulting him at all while picking the XI. I sat beside the captain and told him, ‘I will chair the meeting, along with you and the vice-captain, and let the manager convene it.’ The captain immediately agreed and said, ‘If you are chairing the meeting, I have no issues.’”For Vengsarkar, the danger in leaving the playing XI entirely to the captain and coach is that the two are always closely aligned. That can leave little room for a dissenting view. “If you give the power to pick the XI only to the coach and captain, they generally are always on the same page. That gives them room to bring in their personal likes and dislikes. Let the selector on tour be the neutral voice. If it is a 50-50 call, the selector should always go with the captain. But if you spot something blatantly wrong, he must put his foot down.”Vengsarkar insists this is not an issue restricted to the present set-up. Previous captain-coach combinations, he says, have also enjoyed unhinged power.Without identifying players, he recalled how a cricketer who had scored heavily in an important tournament was relegated to 12th-man duties in the next series because he was viewed as competition for the captain. He cited another instance of a Test cricketer who stood in as captain, won an important Test and soon found himself on the bench. “I would not have allowed it,” he says.As India captain, Vengsarkar did not have the luxury of touring selectors, not least because the BCCI did not have its present financial muscle. “Especially when a series was happening in the West Indies, selectors would not travel. I would ask my vice-captain and another senior player to sit in the meeting along with the manager,” he recalled.His tenure as chief selector also showed that a robust selection structure need not mean confrontation between selector and captain. “There were a lot of questions around Virender Sehwag’s selection for the 2007-08 Australia tour. He had not been part of the England tour earlier that year. But Anil Kumble and I were on the same page and we picked him as the 17th member, despite another opener having scored more runs than him in domestic cricket,” Vengsarkar said.Ultimately, Vengsarkar believes the quality and independence of the individual matter more than merely putting a selector on the plane. “It has become such a lucrative job that sometimes many prefer to stay quiet, take their package and avoid rocking the boat with the coach, captain or board when it comes to selecting or dropping players.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Lot of runs here': Forget the seamer-friendly reputation, New Zealand pacer says Hagley Oval pitch can flatten out
articles.summary: New Zealand pacer Matt Henry has cautioned against reading too much into Hagley Oval's reputation as a seamer-friendly venue ahead of the second Test
articles.body: New Zealand pacer Matt Henry has cautioned against reading too much into Hagley Oval's reputation as a seamer-friendly venue ahead of the second Test against India, which begins in Christchurch on Friday. The warning comes after the opening Test in Wellington turned into a batting-dominated contest despite expectations of assistance for fast bowlers.Only 24 wickets fell across five days in the drawn first Test, with India scoring 720 in their second innings, their highest total overseas. India captain Shubman Gill had expressed his disappointment with the pitch after the teams shook hands with more than 15 overs remaining on the final day.Henry, who has enjoyed success at Hagley Oval, said New Zealand would wait to see how the surface behaves rather than make plans based on its reputation."I think every game's different, every surface you play on is slightly different as well. And I think there's been a lot of runs scored here of late as well," Henry said at a press conference on Wednesday."So for us, it's probably not to get carried away with what it could be and trying to read pitches. It's a pretty fine art to do that."There is reason for New Zealand to be cautious about the conditions. India A and New Zealand A played a four-day match at the venue earlier this month, which also ended in a draw after both teams scored heavily.New Zealand A made 424 in their first innings, with Matt Boyle scoring 110, in reply to India A's 346, which included Dhruv Jurel's 105. India A then scored 282 for two in their second innings, with Yashasvi Jaiswal unbeaten on 155, as the pitch became easier for batting.Henry acknowledged that Hagley Oval has traditionally offered help to fast bowlers, particularly through bounce and carry. However, he said batting conditions can improve as a match progresses."I think traditionally here in New Zealand, the wickets when there's grass on them tend to get better and better, and it's been the same here. It's a good batting venue. Obviously, when there's bounce involved, it's good for the bowler, but from a batting point of view you can score runs quickly as well," he said.The 34-year-old also said batters would need to rely on their defence during difficult periods before looking to score freely."There's moments where you probably have to rely on your defence a little bit, but when you get through those periods, you really can put bowlers under pressure because, like you said, when it flattens out, your margins become pretty small as a bowler."Henry added that playing at home gives New Zealand a degree of familiarity with the ground, though the team would still have to assess the conditions during the match."It's always nice when you're at home and it is a ground you've played a lot of cricket at, so you probably have that element of comfort. You kind of know the ground well and whatnot."But yeah, it's been a great place to play cricket in the past, somewhere I love to play cricket."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Play 20 balls, the score will be different': How Yuvraj Singh's 30-minute call unleashed Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 204
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A half-hour conversation with his idol and mentor Yuvraj Singh proved to be the turning point for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who went on to produce
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A half-hour conversation with his idol and mentor Yuvraj Singh proved to be the turning point for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who went on to produce one of the most extraordinary batting performances in the history of the game, smashing a world-record 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament on Tuesday.The 15-year-old left-hander revealed that he had been struggling with his form and was mentally distracted by a string of low scores before the match. Seeking clarity, he turned to four people, including his father, childhood coach Manish Hoja, former India Under-19 teammate Pratham Jachak and Yuvraj.But it was the conversation with Yuvraj that helped him identify technical flaws, regain confidence and approach his innings with a clearer mindset.In a video shared by the BCCI, Sooryavanshi opened up about the conversation and how the former India all-rounder's advice shaped his approach against the UAE."I spoke to him [Yuvraj Singh] for almost half an hour. He explained a lot to me about batting. I was very worried, so I spoke to him openly. Sir, I am having these problems. When I am going to bat on the wicket. He explained everything to me for half an hour. He told me that if I play 20 balls, the score will be different. He told me a lot of technical things. That helped me a lot today," Sooryavanshi said.'My mind was a little diverted': Yuvraj's advice helped him rediscover his gameSooryavanshi admitted that his recent struggles had left him questioning his approach, with the youngster unable to score runs in his previous two matches and a few domestic outings.He said Yuvraj's advice carried particular weight because of the admiration he has for the former India all-rounder."It's not easy, but as I told you, the last two matches and a few domestic matches, I couldn't score runs. I was a little diverted, and kept asking myself what is happening. But I spoke to Yuvraj sir, he is my idol. If you talk to an idol, you listen to everything he says. I listened to everything he said. He told me a lot of important things," he said.Sooryavanshi also revealed that reviewing videos of his batting helped him recognise the mistakes he had been making. He then tried to implement Yuvraj's suggestions rather than repeat those errors."I saw the video of my batting. I felt that I was making a mistake. I tried not to make those mistake today. I tried to do what he told me to do. He helped me a lot," he added.Backing his strengths after assessing the conditionsThe teenager's innings against the UAE was a remarkable display of power-hitting, but he insisted that his approach was not simply about attacking from the outset. Instead, he first assessed the conditions before deciding to play to his strengths."I just had the mindset to go and see how the wicket was. I went and saw a couple of balls. The ball was coming well on the bat, so I backed my game," he explained.Sooryavanshi also reiterated that he does not consider himself a batter restricted to one format, saying he has the ability to adjust his approach according to the demands of the game."When I was interviewed after the IPL in Ahmedabad, I said that I can play in all three formats. I can change the game according to the situation. I have that much control over my game," he said.He admitted, however, that he had been trying to play the same way in recent matches, even attempting to adopt a longer-format approach when the situation did not necessarily demand it."But in the last two matches, I was trying to play the same way. I was trying to play in a long format. Even today, I had the same mindset. But when I saw the wicket, I didn't feel much help. If I tried to take shots, the ball was coming to my bat. So I backed my strength," he concluded.The result was an astonishing 204 off 53 balls, featuring 28 sixes and seven fours, as India registered a seven-wicket victory over the UAE.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Karnataka lost in transition: R Smaran & co’s SMAT campaign ends prematurely in chaos
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Lack of consistency, a chaotic campaign and an early exit sum up Karnataka’s Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 season.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Lack of consistency, a chaotic campaign and an early exit sum up Karnataka’s Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 season. Although they laboured to a four-wicket win over Rajasthan in Mumbai on Tuesday, the mathematical hope R Smaran and his team clung to evaporated. With Baroda having sealed qualification from Group A, the result had no bearing on Karnataka’s fate. The second spot will be decided by the outcome of the final league encounter between Rajasthan and Bengal.This was Karnataka’s fourth consecutive league-phase exit in the tournament. In the six matches they have played so far, the former champions have hardly looked like contenders. Instead, they have resembled a team caught in a cycle of experimentation. Karnataka have fielded 16 players, with only three — Smaran, Manvanth Kumar and Pravin Dubey — featuring in all six matches.The decision to recall Manish Pandey yielded little, while the persistence with an under-fire Abhinav Manohar did not pay dividends either. The musical chairs at the top of the order only added to the uncertainty, resulting in below-par returns. Tellingly, Karnataka have managed just three half-centuries, with seasoned campaigner Karun Nair accounting for two and Smaran the other.Around 14 players across teams have scored at a strike rate of over 200, but among Karnataka’s top and middle-order batters, Luvnith Sisodia has the best strike rate at 154. Their struggles were also reflected in the team’s totals. Karnataka’s highest score while batting first was 184 in the tournament opener against Bengal, while their lowest was a dismal 95 against Chandigarh.Bowling has also proved to be a major weakness. As many as 12 players have been tried with the ball, but barring Manvanth Kumar, the lone bright spark with 91 runs and 10 wickets, the returns have been largely underwhelming. Abhilash Shetty and Ritesh Bhatkal showed promise in patches, but the rest failed to make a telling impact.It has been one of those rare Karnataka campaigns where the overriding expectation was not a stirring performance, but when the team would implode next.With their campaign ending prematurely, head coach R Vinay Kumar and the selectors have time to take stock of what went wrong, particularly some of the questionable decisions that disrupted the team’s balance. The focus will now shift to the Vijay Hazare Trophy, where Karnataka will hope to start afresh.If this is a team in transition, it is clear that Karnataka are yet to find their way through it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘ICC, boards need to step in’: Harbhajan Singh on India-Pakistan cricket skirmishes
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The last couple of India-Pakistan cricket contests, while they've provided plenty of excitement, have also seen ugly scenes of skirmishes between
articles.body: MUMBAI: The last couple of India-Pakistan cricket contests, while they've provided plenty of excitement, have also seen ugly scenes of skirmishes between the players. On November 14, India's Under-19 players had a go at their Pakistani counterparts, celebrating wildly and overenthusiastically after pipping their arch-rivals by one wicket in a thrilling Under-19 Asia Cup final at Al Amerat in Oman. On November 22 (Sunday) in Doha, players of both India A and Pakistan A (Pakistani Shaheens) exchanged verbal volleys with each other, with India A pacer Harshit Rana involved in heated altercations with the Pakistan players during their Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha, which Pakistan A won by 48 runs.After the ugly scenes witnessed in the Asia Cup Under-19 final, former India skipper Dilip Vengsarkar had told TOI about the need for the BCCI to educate young cricketers at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence about behaving well on the field while playing for India at any level. India's off-spin great Harbhajan Singh has joined the chorus of those voicing their concern at the deteriorating player behaviour during these clashes and has urged the game's authorities — the International Cricket Council and the BCCI — to "step in" to check the trend of players from both countries getting carried away in Indo-Pak cricket matches."Somewhere down the line, the ICC needs to step in. I think it is just getting a bit too much with the reactions. First, Pakistan's boys did it (after beating India Under-19s in the league stage). Then the Indians won and did it. And then yesterday too, whatever happened was not right. If you look at sport as a sport, then it will be far better. See, some amount of chit chat happens, and has been happening for a long time. That should happen also. The game needs a bit of masala (spice) like that. However, it should not reach a point where you feel it is shameful. So, somewhere down the line, I think that the ICC and the respective boards need to put their foot forward and say, 'this is not done.' 'You try hard on the field to win the match for your team, try your best, but after the match, those reactions, I don't think are the right ones. Both from our side and their side," Harbhajan told reporters at an event at the BPGC Golf Course here on Tuesday.Asked specifically about Rana's on-field clashes with Pakistan's players, Harbhajan quipped, "I don't think that should happen. I think it is not setting the right example for the generation coming up."'Have some patience with Team India'While he wasn't critical of India's bowlers' inability to take New Zealand's eight remaining wickets on the final day of the first Test at Wellington, which ended in a draw on Monday, calling the pitch "really flat," Harbhajan, who took 417 wickets in 103 Tests (1998-2015), wasn't entirely convinced about India's decision to shake hands with their Kiwi counterparts even with 15 overs left to be bowled in the last session of the match, and felt that they could have continued bowling. "I thought the pitch was dry and very flat. It's okay. Pitches in Australia and New Zealand tend to be really flat, at times.“I think a lot has been talked about in this game. There were 15 overs left and they declared the game (a draw) before. Yes, you could have tried. You never know. Things move very fast in cricket. But somewhere down the line, you have to be honest with yourself, as a captain and management, whether it was the right decision on that pitch or in that scenario. I think that a lot of thought would have gone into that decision. But if I was part of the management, I would have liked to bowl another 15 overs and give it a try. And let's see. You never know,” Harbhajan said.Recalling how former Australia captain Michael Clarke, with his part-time left-arm spin, had bowled Australia to a win against India in the closing minutes of the controversial Sydney Test in January 2008, taking three for five in 1.5 overs, the former tweaker said, "After everyone else had bowled, Australia introduced Clarke just two overs before (the close of the Test). And nothing was happening. Suddenly he came and he took those two important wickets and they ended up winning that match. So, cricket is a very funny game. Anything can happen."Citing the fighting attitude of his former India spin-bowling partner and ex-India captain Anil Kumble, Harbhajan said, "I have always been a fan of Anil Bhai. And I still say that his attitude was that you have to fight till the last ball. Whether you are bowling or batting or in the field, you have to fight till the last ball. So 90 balls is a lot. I think we should have tried in those 90 balls (to get the remaining five Kiwi wickets). You never know. Maybe the result will come in your favour."Harbhajan defended off-spinner Washington Sundar, who took one for 65 in 35 overs as the Kiwis secured a draw in the first Test. "It's very easy for all of us to pinpoint an individual and say he could have done this or he could have done that. I will put myself in his position. He tried his best. He is young. He is learning. And of course, the more he plays, the more he will learn about these situations. Next time, if he is in such a situation, I am sure he will be able to perform better. So, let's not pinpoint an individual. You win with 11, you lose with 11 and you throw with 11. He must have tried. If it was me, I would have tried as well. So, give him some time. I am sure he will learn and he will get better," Harbhajan stressed.Critics have panned India's inability to close out Test wins in their last two games by taking wickets on the fifth and final day — it happened against Sri Lanka in Colombo in August, and then against New Zealand on the final day of the first Test at Wellington. Harbhajan, though, isn't perturbed and urged fans to "have some patience with the Indian team.""That will happen (closing out Test wins). This is the same team that won in England (India drew the Test series 2-2 last summer in England). Have some patience with the team. We have a trend here. If you don't get a result that we want from the Indian team, then we go after it. Give them a break. They need to 'breathe out' as well. They are on the road continuously. So, give them some break. I'm sure that they'll get the right results for Team India."Would it have made a difference if Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj had played? "Time will tell. You say, what would have happened if Kapil paaji had played? I can't say much about what would have happened. But if he would have played, we would have talked about it. I can't really predict what would have happened if he would have played. If I would have known, I would have called Gautam and asked him to play," Harbhajan retorted.Talking about the ongoing 'Sandpaper-gate' controversy rearing its head in Australian cricket again, Harbhajan felt that it "wasn't a new thing" and that it showed that the Australian team sometimes received far more respect than they deserved."I don't think this is a new thing. This is a very old thing. Pakistan and India have been talking about this for a long time. That this is a reverse swing.We are making such a big thing about this. Australia was doing it before. England was doing it. South Africa was doing it. Wherever there is reverse swing, there must be something with the ball. People are doing it. How much they do it naturally, or the way they have done it with sandpaper, that is a little bad. Naturally, if you go to make the ball reverse, it takes some time to get the ball going. But if you make the ball reverse in the 10th over, then it is understood that there can be nothing but teasing."Australia is not as simple as they used to be. Their players are not as simple as they used to be. I have said this from day one, they should not be given so much respect. They should be given a lot of respect. They have also played the game. They have also done all these things. Now they have been caught or things have come out, they are saying that they did not know. It is not possible that you are living in one house, you are living in another house, you do not know who is living there. Everybody was part of it. I believe. If it is in the team, then it is a collective thing."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Wo paida hua hai samundar ke liye, abhi wo bas ek chote se talab mein hai' - The unprecedented rise of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is explosive, yet his movements are remarkably minimal.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is explosive, yet his movements are remarkably minimal. Few batters have dismantled back-of-a-length and length deliveries down the ground with the kind of authority he has displayed over the last 18 months. He doesn't need a big stride or elaborate trigger movements to generate extraordinary power. Sometimes, all it takes is a shift in weight and those long levers.On Tuesday, the last ball of the 10th over between India A and UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, when he brought up his 150 off just 40 balls, was perhaps the shot of the match. UAE pacer Zahid Ali bowled wide of the off stump, almost on the eighth-stump line. Sooryavanshi, with his long levers, transferred his weight onto the front foot and launched it over deep extra cover for six. A ball that was meant to keep him quiet was sent soaring into the stands.In recent months, Sooryavanshi has left everyone scrambling for superlatives. But Bihar coach Ashok Kumar, who has worked closely with the teenager alongside Manish Ojha, believes the bigger picture is still waiting to unfold."Badi machli hai aur talab chota hai uske liye (He is a big fish in a small pond)," Ashok told TimesofIndia.com."Wo paida hua hai samundar ke liye, abhi wo bas ek chote se talab mein hai (He belongs to the ocean; currently, he is in a small pond)."The evolutionFollowing Virat Kohli’s unbeaten 82 off 51 balls against Australia during the 2016 World T20, Australian cricket writer Gideon Haigh summed up the masterclass with a memorable line in *The Australian*: “Much as the marketers would like to take the cricket out of T20, Kohli keeps putting it back.”Even in T20 cricket, the Kohli-esque style of batting was needed. It survived and thrived despite the 360-degree batting of exemplary players such as AB de Villiers and Suryakumar Yadav.But on Tuesday, the way 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi batted, it looked to be a case of putting the T20 into an ODI, almost video game-esque. At his age, kids do spend a lot of time in front of screens. Vaibhav, however, was tearing helpless UAE bowlers apart in Doha."People complain that there are too many sixes and boundaries and that the grounds are too small. But the reality is that batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker," power-hitting coach Julian Wood told this website.Look at Vaibhav in the IPL. He hit Jasprit Bumrah for six off the first ball and also hit Pat Cummins for six. It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six."If you look at Vaibhav's boundary-hitting patterns, he hits all around the ground, from mid-off all the way around to fine leg. If you're going to bowl wide to him, you'd probably have to bowl wide and full. But you have to execute that delivery perfectly. The problem for bowlers is that when they miss, the ball doesn't just go for four; it goes for six. That puts them under tremendous pressure."Look at Vaibhav in the IPL. He hit Jasprit Bumrah for six off the first ball and also hit Pat Cummins for six. It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six. The mindsets of both batters and bowlers have changed. Batters now think, 'If he misses, I'm going to hit him for six,'" explained Wood.Minimal yet so explosiveZubin Bharucha, one of Sooryavanshi’s mentors, has explained how the teenager manages to hit length deliveries with extraordinary power. He attributes it to Sooryavanshi’s coiled upper body, deep torso bend and weight-loaded back leg, which allow him to get his head outside the line of the ball and bring deliveries outside off stump directly into his eyeline."What enables him to achieve this is a superbly coiled upper half, combined with a considerable bend in his torso at the top of his swing. This allows his head to get outside the line of most deliveries," Bharucha explained.It is all driven by the hip not sliding forward, and this enables him to remain in such a strong coiled position on one leg, from which he can create that hip-and-shoulder separation and attack every ball.With almost all his weight loaded onto the back leg, Sooryavanshi limits forward movement of his hips and avoids the conventional transfer of weight onto the front foot. His front foot often moves only marginally, remaining relatively unloaded, which allows him to finish shots with his foot flared open and ankle turned over."He is effectively operating on one leg, which in itself suggests the weight has to remain back," Bharucha said, explaining why Sooryavanshi can generate power without committing his weight forward.The technique also allows Sooryavanshi to keep his body inside the line of the ball while his hands and bat operate in front of the stumps, a trait Bharucha compares with former greats Don Bradman and Graeme Pollock."This is driven by the deep bend in his back, which allows his hands to operate in front of the stumps, much like some of the greats of the past. They would stand well outside leg stump to ensure the bat operated in front of the stumps while the body remained well inside the line. This resulted in Bradman being dismissed LBW fewer than 10 times in his entire career, while players like Graeme Pollock never got out LBW at all. The deep bend in Sooryavanshi’s back accentuates this trait. Even though he doesn't take an outside-leg-stump guard, he is still able to achieve positions on the crease similar to those of these former greats," he said."It is all driven by the hip not sliding forward, and this enables him to remain in such a strong coiled position on one leg, from which he can create that hip-and-shoulder separation and attack every ball," he added.Bharucha believes this allows Sooryavanshi to avoid committing early to a particular length and instead turn almost every delivery into a scoring opportunity.Blessed with remarkable biomechanicsEarlier this year, after the second IPL playoff between Rajasthan Royals and Gujarat Titans in Chandigarh, Shubman Gill had called Sooryavanshi the "best T20 batter" in the world and explained how blessed the teenager was with his biomechanics."I've not seen anyone bat like the way he bats, and I think in this format, he's right now one of the best batters in the world. It is just not his hitting, but his biomechanics and his hand speed, and, you know, no matter what opposition he plays against. I think, in the years to come, the opposition that he plays against is going to have a tough time against him," he had said.Meanwhile, Julian Wood compares his bat swing with that of a baseball player."If you look at Vaibhav, the way his hands come up is very much like a baseball batter. His bat goes past the perpendicular, which is something you wouldn't necessarily coach. But he can generate serious bat speed. Because his bat goes further past the perpendicular, he has more room to whip his hands through the ball and generate speed," he said.With his 53-ball 204 against the UAE, Sooryavanshi has rewritten the record books in spectacular fashion. Currently, he is not even a regular in T20Is, but he certainly is a big fish in a small pond. He should be thrown into the deep sea. And with age on his side, just imagine how many remarkable things he can do with his bat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ILT20: Gulf Giants crush MI Emirates for second straight win as Shamar Joseph stars with the ball
articles.summary: Dubai: Gulf Giants continued their winning start to the ILT20 Season 5, registering a six-wicket victory over MI Emirates at the Dubai International
articles.body: Dubai: Gulf Giants continued their winning start to the ILT20 Season 5, registering a six-wicket victory over MI Emirates at the Dubai International Stadium on Tuesday after bowling them out for just 91.ILT20 debutant Shamar Joseph and David Wiese claimed three wickets each as MI Emirates were dismissed in 19.3 overs for their lowest total in the league. The 91 was also the joint-second lowest score recorded in Dubai in ILT20 history.Shamar returned figures of 3/9, while Wiese finished with 3/19. Alzarri Joseph, Azmatullah Omarzai and Haider Razzaq picked up a wicket each as Gulf Giants kept MI Emirates in check throughout the innings.The chase was far from straightforward initially, with Gulf Giants losing Rahmanullah Gurbaz (0) and Liam Livingstone (1) inside the first two overs. Omarzai (6) and Dhruv Parashar (15) also fell, leaving the Giants at 50/4.However, Ibrahim Zadran and Heinrich Klaasen steadied the innings with an unbeaten 43-run partnership to take Gulf Giants home in 13.5 overs.Zadran finished on 50 not out from 35 balls, hitting five fours and a six, while Klaasen contributed 16 off 16 deliveries, including a four and a six.Earlier, MI Emirates suffered an early setback when Muhammad Waseem (4) was bowled by Omarzai in the opening over. Shamar then struck twice in the fourth over, removing Kusal Perera (6) and Sanjay Krishnamurthi (0), before dismissing Sherfane Rutherford (1) in the final over of the powerplay.MI Emirates were reduced to 22/4, with Shamar having conceded no runs until his fourth wicket.Nicholas Pooran attempted to revive the innings with Kieron Pollard, but their 29-run stand was broken by Wiese in the 12th over. Pooran departed for 23 off 34 balls, while Pollard was dismissed for 13 by Haider Razzaq in the following over.Rashid Khan (7), Romario Shepherd (13) and Jordan Thompson (3) offered little resistance as MI Emirates continued to lose wickets. Wiese removed Thompson in the 18th over before the innings ended at 91 in 19.3 overs.Player of the Match, Gulf Giants' Shamar Joseph said, "I thought it was simple. I saw Omarzai bowling and the ball was seaming and swinging. It's my debut here, and I'm feeling amazing about what I did. Our chances are good. You meet new people, and a lot of them have played around the world, which helps me. Getting information on the conditions is important."MI Emirates skipper Kieron Pollard said, "We lost a couple of wickets in clusters. You practice for scenarios and conditions, so you don't use pitches as an excuse. I told the bowlers not to look for magic balls. I fielded at short leg numerous times just to try and put pressure on the opponents. There's no need to dissect it much, as it was tough for both sides' batters."Brief scoresMI Emirates 91 in 19.3 overs (Nicholas Pooran 23, Kieron Pollard 13, Romario Shepherd 13, Shamar Joseph 3 for 9, David Wiese 3 for 19)Gulf Giants 93/4 in 13.5 overs (Ibrahim Zadran 50*, Heinrich Klaasen 16*, Dhruv Parashar 15, Jordan Thompson 2 for 27, Fazalhaq Farooqi 1 for 21)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Always wanted Pat to remain captain': Usman Khawaja says he never intended to see Cummins punished amid sandpapergate fallout
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja has backed Cricket Australia's decision to retain Pat Cummins as Test captain amid the renewed controversy over the 2018 ball-tampering
articles.body: Usman Khawaja has backed Cricket Australia's decision to retain Pat Cummins as Test captain amid the renewed controversy over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying he never intended for anyone to face further punishment over Sandpapergate.The controversy resurfaced after Khawaja alleged in his autobiography that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to tamper with the ball during the Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. Cummins denied the claims, and Cameron Bancroft subsequently backed Khawaja's version of events, saying "it was the whole team".Khawaja, speaking on The Grade Cricketer podcast, said he was not seeking sanctions against anyone and was pleased that Cricket Australia had decided to stand by Cummins.“That was never my intention to ever put ... we’ve had enough things in terms of punishments, that have already happened,” Khawaja told The Grade Cricketer podcast.“The really good thing is Todd Greenberg (Cricket Australia CEO) said everyone pretty much has immunity. No one is going to get sanctioned or punished, Pat remains captain.""This was never about me versus Pat, and I know that's what the media wanted, but that was never my goal or intention there," he said.“I always wanted Pat to remain captain. It was never about Pat or Pat losing his captaincy.“I reckon we’re in a really good spot now where it’s a bit freer and I can actually talk about this and I’m not worried about ‘oh I’m going to cook him’ or ‘I’m going to cook this person’. We can actually just talk about what happened.”However, Khawaja said he was surprised by the extent of Cummins' fiery response."I've always loved him as a person and a leader - I was never expecting him to attack me personally like he did," he said."Attack what I said, yeah. Personally, the way he did it and kept going and kept going, I've never seen that side of Pat before."That disappointed me."Khawaja also revealed he had reached out to Cummins before he spoke to the media for 70 minutes at Cricket Central in Sydney on November 13, in an attempt to find "middle ground". "I think people would have respected him for that."He also criticised Cricket Australia for putting Cummins in that position in the first place."This is my issue - Pat was 24 at the time. This wasn't a Patrick Cummins issue," Khawaja said of Sandpapergate."This wasn't about Pat. I think someone at CA should have taken the lead, not Pat."Cricket Australia last week expressed its "unanimous support" for Cummins to continue as Test captain, rejecting suggestions that his integrity had been compromised by the allegations surrounding the 2018 scandal.Cummins had come under scrutiny after Khawaja claimed the entire team was aware of the plan to alter the ball. The Australian captain denied knowing about it during a press conference last week, but Bancroft's subsequent comments added to the controversy.A Cricket Australia investigation into the incident had held only then-captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Bancroft, who used the sandpaper, responsible.Khawaja reignited the debate through his autobiography, with Warner, his close friend, backing his claims. Bancroft later said "it was the whole team" and also expressed feeling "angry and betrayed" by Cummins.Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation into the incident but has set up a forum for players to share their experiences of the 2018 episode.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘A 50-ball 200 is crazy’: Jacob Oram weighs in on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as ODI cricket's 'saviour'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Zealand bowling coach Jacob Oram has been left impressed by the extraordinary rise of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Zealand bowling coach Jacob Oram has been left impressed by the extraordinary rise of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but he has a request for the 15-year-old: save his most destructive innings for someone else.Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm with his astonishing exploits, most recently smashing a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls in a List A match on Tuesday. His innings, which accounted for 204 of India A's 254 runs, powered the side to a seven-wicket victory in a chase of 250 in just 14.2 overs, making the contest look more like a video game than a traditional 50-over match.The knock has also reignited the debate over the relevance of ODI cricket amid the growing popularity of T20s. However, Oram believes it is premature to put the responsibility of saving the format on the shoulders of a teenager."It's a bit cool to call a 15-year-old the saviour. Let's see how it pans out. I understand the public love their T20 cricket and the purists love Test cricket, but I still believe there's a place for 50-over cricket," Oram told PTI.The former New Zealand all-rounder, however, had no reservations about acknowledging the youngster's extraordinary talent."He's (Sooryavanshi) exciting, he's entertaining, and the more of those players involved in cricket, the better it is for the product. I just hope he doesn't get a 50-ball double hundred when we have to bowl against him," he said.'A 50-ball 200 is crazy': Oram marvels at SooryavanshiOram also recalled the teenager's explosive batting against New Zealand in the Wellington T20I, where he scored 45 off just 19 balls."He got one score against us, did he not? (45 in 19 balls in the Wellington T20I) and you could see some glimpses of it. I have seen enough of him on TV in the IPL and elsewhere. This guy is amazing, whatever he is, 15 or 16?. Even if he was 25 or 26, like let us say 10 years older, the age is not a factor; it is about how good he is. A 50-ball 200 is crazy, right? You know, and you sort of wonder where you go from there," Oram told ANI."I have said, though, I just hope it is not against us, and we have to, every time we play him, we have got to make sure we are on our game or else that sort of stuff could happen because he is a talent," he added.Sooryavanshi's numbers underline why opposition bowling attacks are already wary of him. In 16 List A appearances, he has accumulated 805 runs at an average of 50.31 and a strike rate of over 193, including two centuries and two half-centuries. He has also smashed 63 sixes in 16 innings.His exploits in Youth ODIs have been equally remarkable. Representing India Under-19, he has scored 1,412 runs in 25 innings at an average of 56.48 and a strike rate of 165.72, with four centuries and seven fifties. His best score is 175, which came against England in the Under-19 World Cup final earlier this year.In 10 T20Is for India, the left-hander has already scored 295 runs at a strike rate of over 185, including two half-centuries and a highest score of 81.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Goa: The Indian Street Premier League (ISPL) will move to Goa for its fourth season, with the tennis-ball T10 tournament scheduled to run from December 6,
articles.body: Goa: The Indian Street Premier League (ISPL) will move to Goa for its fourth season, with the tennis-ball T10 tournament scheduled to run from December 6, 2026, to January 3, 2027. Eight franchises will compete in 44 matches at the 1919 Sportz Cricket Stadium in Verna.Defending champions Chennai Singams will open the season against last year's runners-up Tiigers of Kolkata on December 6, setting up a rematch of the Season 3 final. Chennai Singams are co-owned by Suriya and Rajdip Gupta, while Tiigers of Kolkata are co-owned by Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Aksha Kamboj.The opening day's fixture will be followed by Majhi Mumbai taking on Ahmedabad Lions on December 4. Srinagar Ke Veer will face Bengaluru Strikers, while Falcon Risers Hyderabad take on Delhi Superheros in the first double-header of the season.The league stage will conclude on December 28, followed by Qualifier 1 on December 29, the Eliminator on December 30 and Qualifier 2 on January 2. The final is scheduled for January 3, 2027.Single-header matches will begin at 8pm, while double-header days will start at 5:30pm.The move to Goa comes as the league looks to expand its reach and strengthen its grassroots talent pathway. Across its first three editions, ISPL has provided a platform for aspiring cricketers from different parts of the country to showcase their abilities in the tennis-ball format.The Season 4 auction also reflected the league's growing commercial footprint, with the eight franchises collectively spending more than ₹10.40 crore.ISPL League Commissioner Suraj Samat said Goa's tourist season offered an opportunity to bring sport and tourism together while continuing to develop the league's talent pool.“Goa offers a fantastic setting for ISPL Season 4, with the schedule also coinciding with the state’s peak tourist season. This presents a natural opportunity for the league to flourish at the intersection of sport and tourism,” Samat said.The league has also revised its player selection process, removing simulation matches and introducing a data-driven system based on performances in local tournaments across the country. The top 500 performers will qualify for the auction pool through points accumulated in these competitions, alongside the top 50 contracted players.The revised process is intended to reduce human
