articles.summary: Usman Khawaja has doubled down on his account of Sandpapergate, tracing Australia's ball-tampering controversy back to a culture of pushing boundaries
articles.body: Usman Khawaja has doubled down on his account of Sandpapergate, tracing Australia's ball-tampering controversy back to a culture of pushing boundaries that, according to him, had been building for years before the incident in Cape Town in 2018. While refusing to name individuals, the former Australian batter explained what he meant when he repeatedly said "everyone knew", arguing that the team had collectively benefited from attempts to generate reverse swing.Speaking on The Grade Cricketer podcast, Khawaja was asked why he was so certain that Australia's bowlers in South Africa were aware of the ball-tampering episode. His latest interview comes amid a divide among those involved in the 2018 infamous incident during Australia's tour of South Africa, with Khawaja, Cameron Bancroft, Chadd Sayers and David Warner maintaining that everybody knew, while Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have continued to deny prior knowledge.Khawaja said he could "sleep very easily at night" knowing the allegations in his book were true.“We can always just talk about the facts in terms of what actually happened at that time. Where I’m at now, I’ve always wanted to take accountability as a team,” he said.Khawaja says 2021 statement created divide within Australia teamThe statement issued by Australia's bowlers in 2021, in which they denied prior knowledge of a foreign substance being taken onto the field during the Cape Town Test, remains a point of disagreement.Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon had made it clear at the time that they had no involvement in Sandpapergate and have continued to stand by that position.“The 2021 (statement). They’re pegged to that. It was a very specific statement. I don’t necessarily disagree with the statement,” Khawaja said.He recalled that when Bancroft had insinuated at the time that everybody knew, he (Khawaja) had spoken to then-coach Justin Langer and wanted the team to take collective responsibility rather than focus on who knew what."At the time, Bancroft insinuated that everybody knew. At the time, I was on the phone to JL (Justin Langer) and telling him we should just take it as a team. It was our opportunity to finish it.'"It wasn't even relevant who knew, who didn't. It was just 'let's take it as a team'."And so for me, when I look back at that, the bowlers then went and put the statement out in 2021, and none of us even knew about it. It just happened. They just did it," Khawaja said on The Grade Cricketer podcast."It kind of left everyone else with our hands in our pockets. It created this separation. They separated themselves from the rest of the team at that point."I talked to Bancroft about this. I was in touch with him all the way from 2018 … He said to me 'that was the loneliest I've ever felt in my life'."Khawaja said he had recently contacted Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg with a proposal for the entire team from the 2018 South Africa tour to accept collective responsibility for the ball-tampering incident. He also drafted a statement and sent it to Greenberg, sharing it with the podcast.“We accept as a group we were ball tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018,” the statement says.“Furthermore, we would like to acknowledge that Steven (Smith), Cameron (Bancroft) and David (Warner) paid an enormous price for the sake of the team, for which we are sorry and eternally grateful.”Khawaja said Greenberg's response was that the proposed statement was likely "not going to fly".'Sandpaper didn't just magically happen': Khawaja traces culture back to 2016Asked again who knew about ball-tampering in South Africa in 2018, Khawaja took the discussion back to 2016, describing what he believed was a culture driven by a "win at all costs" approach that filtered from Cricket Australia to the coaching staff and then the players.“From 2016 and that ‘win at all costs’ mentality all the way to 2018. It came from CA up the top. It filtered down to the coaching staff. The coaching staff pushed it onto the players,” Khawaja told The Grade Cricketer."And it was a really ugly time in more ways than one because, take away the ball tampering stuff, we were a***holes on the field.""I see we because we were a team. I don't say anything, I'm a bit of a mute on the field. Fielding sucks most times. I don't really sledge or anything, it's just not part of my personality."But when I was a part of this team, we were watching it and it was like 'some of the stuff we're saying is so ugly'."It kind of culminated with the Quinton de Kock stuff with Bull (David Warner), the dropping of the ball with Gaz (Nathan Lyon) in front of AB De Villiers' face and the way we were playing, even in the Ashes before, and that was coming from the 'win at all costs, we don't care how you win, just win'."When we talk about ball tampering, sandpaper didn't just magically happen. We didn't go from zero to 100."It was progressive during that time. We kept pushing the boundaries more and more and more during that two-year period."Khawaja said the team's approach had continued to push boundaries during that period and that the ball-tampering episode in South Africa was the culmination of a pattern rather than an isolated incident."For that two years, 'win at all costs', we just kept pushing and pushing to the point where in Port Elizabeth, obviously Warner was one of the guys who managed the ball, but he had too much heat on him.""Unfortunately we went down the sandpaper path and people always ask me 'who knew?' and I'm like, we didn't just start (ball tampering) in South Africa. This was going on consistently for a long period of time."I don't want to speak on anybody's behalf, but it was going on for a long time. We benefited as a team, we were winning games as a team through our tactics with the ball."We win as a team. We lose as a team. We share it as a team. We're doing it to the ball as a team. There's a concerted effort as a team.“For me, over such a long period of time, we all knew we were trying to reverse swing the ball, and we all know how to reverse swing the ball. That’s the context. You can make up your mind on the rest.”Khawaja also said Bancroft had sent him a "Thank You" message after learning what was included in his book.The controversy has put Cummins under pressure since Khawaja alleged that the entire team knew about the plan to alter the ball during the Cape Town Test. Cummins denied being aware of the activity at a press conference last week, but Bancroft subsequently backed Khawaja's account.A Cricket Australia investigation had held only then-captain Steve Smith, deputy David Warner and Bancroft, who was seend using the sandpaper, responsible. Khawaja reignited the debate through his autobiography, with Warner backing his close friend. Bancroft later claimed "it was the whole team" and said he felt "angry and betrayed" by Cummins.Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation but has set up a forum for players to share their experiences of the 2018 incident.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja 'disappointed' by personal attack from Pat Cummins
articles.summary: Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja says it was "never about me versus Pat" as the 2018 sandpapergate scandal rumbles on.
articles.body:
Usman Khawaja says he is "disappointed" by the personal "attack" he faced from Pat Cummins in response to his claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, stating he has "never seen that side" of Australia's Test captain.

Retired batter Khawaja reignited debate around 'sandpapergate' in his autobiography Sabr, claiming the entire Australia team knew about the plan to tamper with the ball in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town.

The incident was widely condemned and led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner, and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft.

Cummins has since dismissed claims the bowlers were involved as "utter nonsense" during a remarkable 68-minute press conference and accused Khawaja of being "casual and flippant" with his friends' reputations and careers.

Khawaja responded on The Grade Cricketer podcast, insisting it was "never about me versus Pat" as he reiterated his support for the 33-year-old to remain as Test captain - but expressed his surprised at Cummins' reaction to his testimony.

"I've always loved him as a person and a leader. I was never expecting him to attack me personally like he did," said Khawaja, who played 36 Tests under Cummins.

"Personally, the way he did it and kept going and kept going, I've never seen that side of Pat before. That disappointed me."

Reiterating his version of events, Khawaja added: "I can sleep very easily at night. I have told the truth."

The sandpaper plot - who was there, who said what?

Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'

Prior to Khawaja's book, Cummins and the other frontline bowlers from Cape Town - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, and Nathan Lyon - had always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper.

In a 2021 statement, the quartet asked for an end to the "rumour-mongering and innuendo", reaffirming their stance that they "did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field" until images appeared on the ground's big screen.

While neither supporting nor dismissing their position, Khawaja said the bowlers are "pegged" to their words from five years ago and their position created a divide in the Australia dressing room.

"It's not like they told us they were going to do it," added Khawaja. "They just did it.

"They separated themselves from the rest of the team at that point."

Khawaja also revealed he has written an apology statement on behalf of the team and sent it to Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg in an attempt to find a way to "meet in the middle".

The statement read: "We accept and acknowledge as a team that we knew we were ball-tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa [in] 2018. Whether it was sandpaper or by any other means is irrelevant.

"We knew what we were doing and we take full responsibility as a team and a squad for our actions, something we should have done eight years ago.

"Furthermore, we would like to acknowledge that Steven (Smith), Cameron (Bancroft), and David (Warner) paid an enormous price for the sake of the team, for which we are sorry and eternally grateful."

While Greenberg replied to say he did not think the statement was "gonna fly", Khawaja said the pair are confident of bringing the saga to an end.

"I've still got this pipe dream of accountability," said Khawaja. "He said, 'Look, no matter what it was at least we can look each other in the eye and say that we are trying everything possible to try to move Australian cricket forward.'

"The really good thing that came out is Todd Greenberg said everyone pretty much has immunity.

"I reckon we're in a really good spot now where it's a little bit freer, where we can actually talk about this."

articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah closes in on Mitchell Starc for No.1 spot as Yashasvi Jaiswal joins Rishabh Pant, Shubman Gill in ICC Test top 10
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah is closing in on Australia's Mitchell Starc at the top of the ICC Test bowling rankings, having climbed
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah is closing in on Australia's Mitchell Starc at the top of the ICC Test bowling rankings, having climbed three places to share second position in the latest update. India's batting trio of Rishabh Pant, Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal are in the top 10, underlining the country's strong presence among the leading Test performers.Bumrah's five-wicket match haul in the first Test against New Zealand, which ended in a draw, earned him a significant jump in the latest standings. He is now level with England's Ollie Robinson in second place, with Starc continuing to lead the bowling rankings.The Indian fast bowler is just 25 rating points behind the Australian left-armer, keeping him firmly in contention for the No.1 position.South Africa's Kagiso Rabada has also made progress, climbing two places to sixth following his eight-wicket haul against Bangladesh. Pakistan fast bowler Mohammad Abbas has gained two spots to move to 12th after his impressive showing against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi.Three Indians in top 10 of Test batting rankingsThere has been movement among India's leading batters as well, with Pant, Gill and Jaiswal all making gains in the latest update.Pant has climbed one place to sixth after his impressive 128 in the first Test against New Zealand. Gill, who scored 98 in the match, has moved up three places to seventh, while Jaiswal has gained five spots to reach ninth.England's Harry Brook and Joe Root continue to occupy the top two positions in the Test batting rankings, but South Africa captain Temba Bavuma has made one of the biggest advances, climbing to third after remaining unbeaten on 68 against Bangladesh.India's KL Rahul has gained four places to move to 25th, while Devdutt Padikkal has made an impressive 15-place jump to 39th after scoring 80.New Zealand's Glenn Phillips has climbed 13 places to a career-best 17th, while Henry Nicholls has moved up 10 spots to 30th. Bangladesh's Towhid Hridoy has gained 28 places to reach 33rd after scoring 137, while Litton Das has climbed nine spots to 24th.England stars make gains in white-ball rankingsThe latest ICC update has also brought significant changes to the ODI and T20I rankings, with several England players registering career-best positions following their performances against Australia.Ben Duckett has climbed three places to fourth in the ODI batting rankings after scoring a superb 133 in England's series-deciding victory in Hobart, which helped them clinch the three-match series 2-1.Will Jacks has moved up five places to 47th among ODI batters, while Gus Atkinson and Liam Dawson have reached career-best positions among bowlers, climbing to 23rd and 39th respectively.In the T20I rankings, England spinner Adil Rashid has moved up one place to second among bowlers. Phil Salt has gained two spots to sixth among batters, while Tom Banton has made a substantial 26-place jump to 34th. Sam Curran has also climbed 12 places to share 45th among T20I bowlers.The five-match T20I series between Australia and England is currently level at 1-1, with the latest rankings reflecting the visitors' strong individual performances in the white-ball formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Punjab Kings appoint Paras Mhambrey as fast bowling coach ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: Punjab Kings (PBKS) have appointed Paras Mhambrey as their fast bowling coach ahead of IPL 2027, the franchise announced on Wednesday.
articles.body: Punjab Kings (PBKS) have appointed Paras Mhambrey as their fast bowling coach ahead of IPL 2027, the franchise announced on Wednesday.Mhambrey's appointment comes after PBKS parted ways with bowling coach James Hopes and fielding coach Brad Haddin last month. He will work under head coach Ricky Ponting, having previously been part of the Australian's coaching setup at Mumbai Indians.Mhambrey was India's bowling coach under Rahul Dravid from 2021 to 2024. During this period, he was part of the coaching staff that guided India to the 2023 ODI World Cup final at home and the 2024 T20 World Cup title in the Caribbean.He has also worked with Mumbai Indians in two stints. Mhambrey returned to the franchise after his time with the Indian team but left last month following a restructuring of its coaching staff.PBKS are yet to win an IPL title, having finished runners-up twice. They lost the 2014 final to Kolkata Knight Riders before going down to Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2025.The franchise had a strong start to IPL 2026, winning six of its first seven matches, while the other game was washed out. However, PBKS could not maintain that run in the second half of the league stage. They managed only one more win in their remaining seven matches and failed to qualify for the playoffs.Led by India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, PBKS will enter the December 16 auction in Goa with 19 players retained. They have a purse of Rs 18.60 crore and six slots to fill, including two for overseas players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Time to hang them up': Stuart MacGill tells Nathan Lyon to make way for Australia's next generation of spinners
articles.summary: Former Australia leg-spinner Stuart MacGill believes Nathan Lyon's time in the Test side is up, going a step further by suggesting the veteran should
articles.body: Former Australia leg-spinner Stuart MacGill believes Nathan Lyon's time in the Test side is up, going a step further by suggesting the veteran should consider retiring from first-class cricket to make way for younger spinners chasing international ambitions.MacGill believes the 39-year-old is occupying a place that could be better utilised by emerging talent, both at the national and state levels, and has questioned whether Lyon still merits a place in Australia's plans."I've been of this mind for quite some time - nothing personal against Nathan, but I just think that he's just holding a place at the moment," MacGill said on the Chin Music podcast. "I'll go as far as to say I think he's a placeholder in the NSW team as well."Lyon has come under increasing scrutiny following Australia's recent tour of South Africa, where he was left out of the second Test in Gqeberha before managing just four wickets in 67 overs in the third Test in Cape Town. South African spinner Simon Harmer, meanwhile, claimed 10 wickets in the match.MacGill wants opportunities for younger spinnersMacGill believes Lyon's continued presence in the New South Wales side is restricting opportunities for 24-year-old Tanveer Sangha, who has represented Australia in white-ball cricket but is looking to establish himself in the longer format."I'm not sure whether or not now is the right time for him to go 'You know what? I've been a great bowler for Australia, I've taken a lot of wickets for Australia and the various states that I've played for, but maybe it's time to hang them up'," he said."I'd just like to see some other guys get opportunities for NSW. If he's not in the Australian team, he's keeping guys like Tanveer (Sangha) out of the NSW team, which is a shame," the 55-year-old added.MacGill also questioned the need to carry Lyon in the squad when Australia already have other spin options, including Matt Kuhnemann and Cooper Connolly, as well as former New Zealand captain and spin great Daniel Vettori on the coaching staff."You've got Dan Vettori as part of that group. I don't think you need to take up one of the playing spots with a guy that's not going to play," he said. "You've got Kuhnemann, Connolly..."O'Keefe backs Lyon for India tourFellow former Australia spinner Steve O'Keefe disagreed with MacGill, arguing that Lyon's experience could prove invaluable during Australia's upcoming five-Test tour of India. However, he acknowledged that the veteran's place should not be taken for granted."I'd like to keep Nathan Lyon in the team, and this is one of the main reasons: they're going to go to India, and I think having an experienced spinner there for five Tests will be really important," O'Keefe said.Lyon has taken 577 wickets in 145 Tests, making him Australia's second-highest wicket-taker in the format. Australia are scheduled to announce their squad for the four-Test series against New Zealand, beginning December 9, after the ongoing Sheffield Shield round.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Imesha Dulani, Sathya Sandeepani star as Sri Lanka beat Ireland to win Women's Emerging Nations Trophy
articles.summary: Sri Lanka produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Ireland by six wickets and clinch the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 on
articles.body: Sri Lanka produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Ireland by six wickets and clinch the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 on Wednesday. Imesha Dulani starred with an unbeaten 44 as Sri Lanka comfortably chased down the 97-run target in just 12.4 overs in the final at the Karwan Sports Club.The victory marked Sri Lanka's first title in the tournament's history, succeeding Thailand, who won the inaugural edition in 2025.Sri Lanka's bowlers bundle out Ireland for 96After opting to bat first, Ireland endured a disastrous start, losing captain Gaby Lewis in the opening over at 5/1. The early setback soon turned into a collapse as they slipped to 10/2 before struggling to recover. Sri Lanka's disciplined bowling attack kept the pressure firmly on Ireland, reducing them to 54/6 inside 12 overs.Alana Dalzell emerged as Ireland's top scorer with 24 off 25 deliveries, while Louise Little contributed 15 off 17 balls. Georgina Dempsey also chipped in with 13, but Ireland failed to build meaningful partnerships and were eventually bowled out for 96 in 19.3 overs.Sathya Sandeepani was the standout performer with the ball, claiming four wickets for just 13 runs in her four overs. Kavisha Dilhari, Sugandika Kumari, Nimasha Meepage and Chethana Vimukthi picked up a wicket apiece, while two run-outs further dented Ireland's innings.Imesha Dulani guides Sri Lanka to titleChasing 97, Sri Lanka made an aggressive start but suffered a brief setback after Sanjana Kavindi departed for 25 off 22 balls. Captain Harshitha Samarawickrama was dismissed for a golden duck on the following delivery, leaving Sri Lanka at 35/2.Ireland attempted to stage a comeback through Kia McCartney and Cara Murray, who picked up two wickets each to reduce Sri Lanka to 69/4 in the ninth over.However, Dulani held her nerve and ensured there were no further hiccups. She remained unbeaten on 44, while Dilhari provided valuable support with an unbeaten 16 off just 10 deliveries.The pair stitched together an unbroken 30-run partnership to take Sri Lanka to 99/4 in 12.4 overs, sealing a convincing six-wicket victory and the championship trophy.Brief ScoresIreland Women: 96 all out in 19.3 overs (Alana Dalzell 24, Louise Little 15; Sathya Sandeepani 4/13) lost to Sri Lanka Women: 99/4 in 12.4 overs (Imesha Dulani 44*, Sanjana Kavindi 25; Kia McCartney 2/16, Cara Murray 2/38) by six wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: T20 Blast: Northants to begin title defence at Hampshire
articles.summary: Northamptonshire Steelbacks will begin their T20 Blast defence at Hampshire, in a repeat of last season's final.
articles.body:
Northamptonshire Steelbacks will begin the defence of their T20 Blast crown with a repeat of last season's final, travelling to Hampshire Hawks on Friday, 21 May.

It is one of nine back-to-back men's and women's matches happening across the opening weekend of the 2027 campaign as the competition celebrates its 25th edition.

Every county will host at least one double-header next season with Glamorgan, Hampshire, Surrey and Yorkshire each staging a maximum of six at their home venues.

Women's champions Nottinghamshire Outlaws - who have rebranded from The Blaze - begin their season at home to Yorkshire.

Newly-rebranded Bristol Lions will be in action on opening night, with the men's side hosting Durham at the Seat Unique Stadium.

The competition will run for eight weeks, with Men's Finals Day set to return to Edgbaston on Saturday, 17 July, while the Women's Finals Day will take place the following day at Trent Bridge.

Full list of 2027 Men's T20 Blast fixtures

Full list of 2027 Women's T20 Blast fixtures

Gloucestershire renamed Bristol Lions for T20 Blast

Next year's edition will include 68 double-headers across the men's and women's competitions - a record for the domestic game.

There will also be an increase on matches played over the weekend, with 88% of next season's T20 Blast fixtures taking place on either a Friday, Sunday or Bank Holiday Monday.

The group stage will end on Sunday, 11 July with a full programme of nine double-headers across the men's and women's competitions.

The format of the men's groups will remain the same as last season with six sides split into three groups - north, central and south.

Each men's side will play 12 matches in the group stage - 10 home and away against counties in the same group and two against sides from outside their group.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) have also confirmed no county will play matches on consecutive days in the competition next year.

Neil Snowball, ECB managing director, competitions and major events, said: "The 25th season of the T20 Blast is a landmark moment for the world's original professional T20 competition and a chance to celebrate its incredible history.

"We're excited to build on that heritage with a fixture schedule that gives fans more opportunities to attend and watch the T20 Blast at the times they prefer, while also creating a player-friendly calendar with no back-to-back matches."

Wednesday, 14 July: Men's quarter-finals

Saturday, 17 July: Men's Finals Day (Edgbaston)

articles.title: 'Ridiculous stage white-ball cricket has reached': Sanjay Manjrekar raises concern after Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's  204
articles.summary: Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar has heaped praise on teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi following his extraordinary batting display against the
articles.body: Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar has heaped praise on teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi following his extraordinary batting display against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026. However, while acknowledging the youngster's exceptional talent, Manjrekar also raised concerns over the growing imbalance between bat and ball in white-ball cricket.Sooryavanshi produced a record-breaking performance in Doha on Tuesday, smashing a sensational 204 off just 53 deliveries to help India A chase down a target of 250 in only 14.2 overs. His innings featured seven boundaries and a staggering 28 sixes, making it one of the most remarkable knocks in List A cricket.Reacting to the teenager's extraordinary display, Manjrekar took to X and questioned whether the current direction of white-ball cricket was genuinely what fans wanted to see."There is something special about Vaibhav no doubt about that. But what he did is another reminder of the ridiculous stage white ball cricket has reached. It's a fallacy to think that this is what fans want. It's a game of bat & ball. Not just bat," Manjrekar wrote.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 204 against UAEThe 15-year-old left-hander unleashed a stunning assault on the UAE bowling attack, reaching his century in just 28 balls to register the fastest hundred in List A cricket. He went on to complete his 150 in 40 deliveries before bringing up his double century off just 52 balls.In the process, Sooryavanshi broke several records, including the previous fastest List A century held by Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk, who had reached the milestone in 29 balls.His 28 sixes were also the most by a batter in a single innings in professional cricket. He finished with a strike rate of 384.90, setting another List A record for the highest strike rate in an innings of 100 or more runs.India A eventually reached 254/3 in just 14.2 overs to register a seven-wicket victory, chasing down the UAE's total of 249/8 with 214 balls to spare.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: '28-ball hundred to double ton': Tilak Varma stunned by Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 204, explains Pakistan loss comments
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma was left amazed by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's extraordinary 53-ball 204 against the UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma was left amazed by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's extraordinary 53-ball 204 against the UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup, admitting that even the team did not expect the 15-year-old to produce such a breathtaking performance.Sooryavanshi smashed the fastest List A century, reaching the milestone in just 28 balls, before completing his double hundred off 52 deliveries. His innings, which included a staggering 28 sixes, powered India A to a seven-wicket victory as they chased down 250 in just 14.2 overs in their Group B encounter on Tuesday."It was an absolutely fantastic innings to watch. A 28-ball hundred is something! Everyone knows that he will break the record, but we haven't thought that he will break it in this match only. Credit goes to him. From 28-ball hundred to double ton, it was tremendous to watch," Tilak said.The India A captain also offered an amusing insight into how the team reacts to Sooryavanshi's extraordinary hitting, revealing that the youngster is encouraged to play his natural game without worrying about taking singles."Hum usko kuch bolte nahi hai. Usse na niche se single lena nahi aata, usko hum bolte hai bhai tera jo game hi khel. Hum uska chauka celebrate nahi kar rahe the, aur 6 gaye toh hum puchte hai door gaye ki nahi? 30 sixes yaar, soch..180 runs toh uska udhar hi ho gaya," he said.Sooryavanshi turns the game into a six-hitting spectacleHaving fallen cheaply in his first two outings, Sooryavanshi made up for those disappointments in spectacular fashion, taking apart the UAE bowling attack with an astonishing display of power-hitting.The left-hander reached his first hundred off 28 balls and needed just another 24 deliveries for his second hundred. He bettered Jake Fraser-McGurk's record for the fastest List A century by a ball and comfortably surpassed Chad Bowes' 103-ball double hundred for Canterbury.His 28 sixes were the most in a single innings in professional cricket, while India A completed the chase in just 14.2 overs after UAE had posted 249/8, with Harpreet Singh Bhatia top-scoring with 130.Tilak explains comments after Pakistan defeatTilak also clarified his post-match remarks following India A's 48-run defeat against Pakistan A, which attracted criticism from sections of fans.The India A skipper had scored 100 off 149 balls in the 314-run chase but felt the team could have won had another batter stayed with him longer. Explaining his approach, he said the regular fall of wickets and the changing nature of the pitch had forced him to bat deep rather than attack from the outset."I always say, I am players' captain. In my perspective, we lost Vaibhav early then we had a partnership with Abhishek, then we lost wickets at regular intervals and we were 6 wickets down in no time. I could also start hitting from the first ball, but at that time the pitch was getting difficult," he said after the UAE game.Tilak also praised Shahbaz Ahmed, whose 56 helped him stitch together a 112-run seventh-wicket partnership."No one had thought that Shehbaz will come and start playing like that, it was a fantastic knock. I even told him in the dressing room that he won my heart with the knock. Unfortunately he got out, otherwise he would have finished the game for us," he said.The captain insisted that his comments were intended to explain the team's batting approach and not single out anyone for the defeat."I told the team after the match that one game won't define us and everyone in our team is a match-winner. My team knows I backed the team, outside noise don't bother me much," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why Ben Stokes could become the costliest player at the IPL auction
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former England captain Ben Stokes could emerge as the costliest buy at the upcoming IPL mini-auction, scheduled to be held in Goa on December
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former England captain Ben Stokes could emerge as the costliest buy at the upcoming IPL mini-auction, scheduled to be held in Goa on December 16. The 35-year-old is listed at the highest base price of Rs 2 crore.Stokes, who has represented three IPL franchises in the past, is expected to trigger a bidding war between Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) and Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR). The two franchises will enter the mini-auction with purses of Rs 47.45 crore and Rs 41.65 crore, respectively.In 2017, Stokes was the most expensive overseas player at the auction when he was bought for Rs 14.5 crore by the then Sanjiv Goenka-owned Pune franchise. The all-rounder scored 316 runs and picked up 12 wickets in 12 outings. Now, with LSG looking for a captain and someone who can provide stability in the middle order while also delivering four overs, Stokes could prove to be a gold-dust acquisition.In Aiden Markram, Mitchell Marsh and Nicholas Pooran, LSG have a power-packed top order but a relatively fragile middle order. They have already acquired Sam Curran in a trade from the Rajasthan Royals, but will still be looking for a captain. Since reaching the IPL playoffs in 2022 and 2023, LSG have finished seventh in 2024 and 2025, before improving a touch to fifth in 2026.Meanwhile, KKR, after releasing their captain Ajinkya Rahane, will also enter the mini-auction hoping to find a leader. The franchise has released 12 players, including four overseas and eight Indian players.With Stokes now retired from international cricket and available for the entire IPL season, landing him could be a significant boost for either franchise. His presence could immediately strengthen their title ambitions and give them a player around whom the next cycle (2026-30) could be built.The 35-year-old has not played a T20 since the 2024 edition of The Hundred, where he picked up a hamstring injury. He was due to appear in the SA20 for MI Cape Town in early 2025 but was ruled out after another hamstring injury.Stokes flies safely under IPL rulesUnlike his ex-England teammate Harry Brook -- who is serving a two-season ban for withdrawing before the tournament began -- Stokes has safely entered the mini-auction.Stokes, who has played for Rising Pune Supergiant, Rajasthan Royals and Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, didn't enter the 2025 mega auction. According to the rules, he was ineligible for the 2026 season but can, and has, enter the 2027 mini-auction.After retiring from international cricket in June, Stokes returned to playing for Durham and helped them secure promotion to Division One of the County Championship. However, he has hinted that he could miss at least the first six rounds of County matches if he is picked at the IPL mini-auction.Stokes has played 45 matches in the IPL and has amassed 935 runs, including two hundreds. With the ball, he's taken 28 wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Shakib, Mustafizur not among Bangladeshi players on 2027 IPL auction list
articles.summary: Eleven Bangladeshi players have entered their names for the auction, a year after Mustafiz’s expulsion from the league.
articles.body:
Former captain Shakib Al-Hasan and fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman are notable absentees on the list of 11 Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the Indian Premier League’s (IPL) upcoming player auction, as tensions continue to simmer between the South Asian neighbours.

Top-order batter Towhid Hridoy leads the players, named on a list released on Wednesday, who are seeking a place in the world’s most lucrative cricket franchise league, a year after Mustafiz’s controversial removal from the IPL.

The 11 Bangladeshis feature on an initial list of 1,220 players for the December 16 mini auction in Goa, although the pool will be trimmed before franchises make their selections, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) said.

“With 184 players already retained or picked by the franchises ahead of the auction, a maximum of 66 slots, including 25 overseas slots, are available to be filled,” the BCCI said in a statement.

Apart from Hridoy, who is enjoying great run-scoring form, Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, and Taskin Ahmed are on the list, according to cricket news outlet Cricinfo.

The presence of Bangladeshi names on the draft auction comes as a surprise, months after the country’s expulsion from the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup , cohosted by India.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) refused to send its team to India over security concerns, which followed a fallout over star pacer Mustafizur’s removal from the Kolkata Knight Riders’ roster upon the BCCI’s instructions.

Though the BCCI gave no clear reason for his expulsion, the board said it was due to “developments all around” – an apparent reference to the tensions between India and Bangladesh that soared following the ouster of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024, who then received exile in New Delhi.

The relationship between India and Bangladesh remains tense over Dhaka’s extradition request for Hasina, which New Delhi has yet to comply with.

Among the more than 1,000 players listed for auction, England all-rounder Ben Stokes is among the high-profile names, with a base price of $216,900.

Indian players dominate the initial list, accounting for 939 registrations.

Australia leads the overseas contingent with 53 players, followed by South Africa (40), West Indies (36), New Zealand (25) and Afghanistan (23).

The list also includes players from emerging cricket nations, with 13 registrations from the United States, and 10 each from the United Arab Emirates and Nepal.

Franchises will finalise their squads after the auction, which will determine the player pool for next year’s edition of the competition.

articles.title: Wiaan Mulder strikes for South Africa to leave Bangladesh trailing by 294 runs at lunch on day three
articles.summary: CENTURION, South Africa (AP) — Wiaan Mulder picked 2-16 as Bangladesh was down to 109-3 (31 overs) in its second innings at lunch on day three of the second...
articles.body:
CENTURION, South Africa (AP) — Wiaan Mulder picked 2-16 as Bangladesh was down to 109-3 (31 overs) in its second innings at lunch on day three of the second cricket test against South Africa.

The Proteas declared on their overnight score of 494-7 (115 overs) , taking a 403-run first innings' lead. Bangladesh was out for 91 in its first innings on day one.

At lunch, Najmul Hossain Shanto (12 not out) and Towhid Hridoy (23 not out) were unbeaten, with the visitors still trailing by a mammoth 294 runs.

With South Africa declaring, day three began with Bangladesh's second innings and it had a good opening stand.

Tanzid Hasan Tamim and Mahfijul Islam added 58 off 87 balls for the first wicket. Their 50-stand came off 73 balls and they nearly batted out the first session without loss.

Tamim scored 29 off 48 balls and was first out, caught behind off Mulder an over before drinks.

Mulder then got Mominul Haque an over later. Haque was caught behind for a five-ball duck as Bangladesh was down to 58-2.

Islam scored 38 off 62 balls and hit seven fours, before he was out lbw to Marco Jansen in the 22nd over. He had added 20 with Shanto for the third wicket, but the budding partnership was cut short.

The opener reviewed, but DRS went against him and stayed in the bowler's favor.

Bangladesh crossed 100 before lunch, as Shanto and Hridoy added 31 off 55 balls for the unbeaten fourth wicket.

South Africa leads the two-match series 1-0, after it won the first test in Johannesburg by nine wickets .

articles.title: Ben Stokes eligible, Harry Brook banned: Why two England stars have different IPL 2027 auction status?
articles.summary: Two England cricketers, two contrasting IPL stories.
articles.body: Two England cricketers, two contrasting IPL stories. While former England captain Ben Stokes has registered for the IPL 2027 mini-auction, current skipper Harry Brook remains ineligible to enter the auction, even if he wishes to do so.Interestingly, the contrasting situations of the two players stem from different clauses in the BCCI's IPL player regulations. While Stokes missed the 2025 mega-auction to prioritise his workload and international commitments, Brook withdrew after being bought by Delhi Capitals at the same auction.The difference between not registering for an auction and withdrawing after being picked has proved significant, with the latter carrying a much stricter penalty.Why is Ben Stokes eligible for the IPL 2027 auction?The BCCI introduced a regulation ahead of the 2025 mega-auction making it mandatory for overseas players to register if they wanted to remain eligible for the following year's auction.The rule states: "Any Overseas Player will have to register for the Big Auction. In case the overseas player doesn't register, then he will be ineligible to register in the following year's player auction."Stokes did not register for the 2025 mega-auction as he wanted to manage his workload and prioritise his England career. Consequently, he was ineligible for the 2026 mini-auction. However, the restriction applied only to the following year's auction. With that period now over, the former England captain is eligible to register for the IPL 2027 mini-auction at a base price of Rs 2 crore.Why is Harry Brook banned from the IPL until 2028?Brook's situation is different. Delhi Capitals signed the England batter for Rs 6.25 crore at the 2025 mega-auction. However, he withdrew before the season began. The BCCI regulations clearly outline the consequences of such a decision:"Any player who registers in the player auction and after getting picked at the auction, makes himself unavailable before the start of the season, will get banned from participating in the tournament and player auction for 2 Seasons."As a result, Brook was handed a two-season ban, ruling him out of the IPL 2026 and 2027 seasons. He will only become eligible to return after the completion of the 2027 season.Why did the BCCI introduce the two-season ban? The BCCI introduced stricter regulations following repeated instances of overseas players withdrawing from the IPL after being picked at auctions. Franchises had raised concerns over players making themselves unavailable after securing contracts, leaving teams with limited time to find suitable replacements.Several high-profile overseas cricketers, including Jason Roy and Alex Hales, had previously withdrawn after being picked at auctions. The repeated instances prompted franchises to seek stricter measures to protect their investments and ensure greater squad stability. Under the revised regulations, a player who withdraws after being bought faces a two-season ban unless the withdrawal is due to a verified injury or medical condition.Ben Duckett, Mitchell Starc and other overseas withdrawal casesBrook is not the only England player to have faced consequences after withdrawing from the IPL. Ben Duckett, who was bought by Delhi Capitals for Rs 2 crore ahead of the 2026 season, also withdrew to prioritise his England commitments and faces the two-season penalty.Other notable withdrawal cases include:Ben Stokes: Withdrew ahead of IPL 2024 to manage his workload and fitness after being associated with Chennai Super Kings.Mitchell Starc: Missed the 2017 season with Royal Challengers Bangalore to manage his workload.Jason Roy and Alex Hales: Previously withdrew from IPL campaigns after being picked at auctions.Wanindu Hasaranga's case: Why injury withdrawals are differentSri Lanka all-rounder Wanindu Hasaranga offers another example of how injury-related withdrawals are treated differently.Hasaranga missed the 2024 season after being signed by Sunrisers Hyderabad and was also unavailable for Lucknow Super Giants during IPL 2026 because of a hamstring injury. Unlike voluntary withdrawals, verified injury-related unavailability does not automatically trigger the two-season ban.Hasaranga has subsequently registered for the IPL 2027 mini-auction at a base price of Rs 2 crore.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WBBL 2026: Deandra Dottin out to 'free ball' in historic decision
articles.summary: Brisbane's Sarah Glenn bowls to an empty set of stumps to dismiss Melbourne Renegade's Deandra Dottin after she is deemed too slow to reach the crease and face her first delivery.
articles.body:
A bizarre dismissal in the Women's Big Bash saw Brisbane Heat's Sarah Glenn bowling to an empty set of stumps , external after Melbourne Renegades new batter Deandra Dottin was ruled to have taken too long to face the delivery.

Experienced West Indies all-rounder Dottin walked out to bat, following the dismissal of Georgia Wareham, with her equipment in disarray and proceeded to adjust her helmet and begin putting on her gloves after arriving in the middle.

Rules introduced before the 2021 WBBL season to speed up play state that an incoming batter must be ready to face - or the non-striker to receive - the next delivery within 75 seconds of a dismissal or retirement.

The umpires adjudged Dottin to have exceeded this time limit and instructed her to stand aside from stumps, while awarding Glenn a free ball.

Glenn hit the middle and leg stumps to remove Dottin for a golden duck. The bowler was initially uncertain how to celebrate - she laughed and covered her face with her hands - before being mobbed by her team-mates.

However, despite the wicket reducing the Renegades to 97-5 with 41 runs needed from 34 balls, they completed their chase of 138 off the final delivery of the match to win by three wickets.

articles.title: Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja 'hurt' by 'personal attacks' from Pat Cummins as he details Cameron Bancroft relationship
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja hopes there is collective responsibility for the Sandpapergate scandal in time and says current captain Pat Cummins still has the "opportunity of power"; former batter says Cameron Bancroft feels like a "different person" after finally telling his side of ball-tampering saga
articles.body:
Khawaja made the allegations in his autobiography Sabr and they have since been backed up by David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of the players, along with then-skipper Steve Smith, who were slapped with bans following the ball-tampering plot in South Africa.

Cummins, part of the Australia bowling attack on that tour eight years ago, insisted he was not privy to the scheme when he and fellow quicks Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, as well as spinner Nathan Lyon, released a joint-statement in 2021.

He then categorially denied knowledge earlier this month in a 68-minute press conference in which he accused Khawaja of being "casual" with people's lives.

Khawaja said in a chat with Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain: "It was the most surprised I've been for a long time. I wasn't expecting that [from Cummins] whatsoever.

"I thought Pat had this really great opportunity to come out and bring everyone together. He's such a great leader. I've said in the book that I love the person he is, love the leader he is, so I thought if anyone can bring us together, it's Pat.

"I had hoped that he would - I text him before, trying do anything I could to make it easier, to do something to bring everyone in - but I realised that wasn't going to happen when he first started talking, so that was really sad.

"Then obviously the personal attacks were sad. I'm not going to lie about that, they hurt from a friend, someone you really respect. That wasn't very Pat Cummins-like, very different to the Pat Cummins I know, and it's hard for me to judge him on that.

"I know Pat, I know his family. They're beautiful, so it was really hard to reconcile the Pat I knew and the Pat that was attacking me personally rather than attacking what I'm saying. That was by far one of the toughest days I've ever experienced.

"I'll caveat that by saying that I have nothing but love for Pat. I don't judge people on certain instances or whatnot. That's not how I live my life. That's not how I function.

"Right now, are we talking? No, not really, but I've still got a lot of hope in my heart that at some stage if there's anyone that can bring everyone together, it's Pat. He's got the opportunity of power, whether it's now or later.

"But I think there was a perfect opportunity there if he took a softer route. He took a real harsh route and I think because of that everything just blew up after that like even more."

'It doesn't feel there is an ending right now and that sucks'

Khawaja wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the sandpaper plot at the time but says he was talked out of it by Smith as only the skipper, Warner and Bancroft - the player caught on camera looking to manipulate the ball - were suspended.

The 39-year-old, who retired from international cricket following Australia's 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, is hopeful "accountability" will eventually come.

He said: "For me it was about the team, Cricket Australia, coming together and saying, 'look, we didn't live up to our standards, we didn't live up to our values and three guys suffered for that'.

"I think there is a way to collectively take this still.

"Will everyone like agree on this? I can't see it happening now the way it's gotten, but for me the middle ground is the collective responsibility and accountability as a team.

"We win together, we lose together, we get caught for ball tampering, we take it together. I think that's achievable, but I can't speak for everyone.

"It doesn't feel there is an ending right now and that sucks for everyone."

Khawaja explained that he became extremely close to Bancroft on the 2019 Ashes tour of England when the latter returned to the side for the first time since 'Sandpapergate' and played what, as things currently stand, are his final two Test matches.

Bancroft's detail-filled, 4,000-word-plus account of the sandpaper deception dropped in the West Australian newspaper on the day of Australia's third ODI against in Hobart, adding even more intrigue to a story that has rocked, and gripped, cricket.

Khawaja said of his relationship with Bancroft: "In the 2019 Ashes, we both played, we got both got dropped and we would play Uno pretty much every day. If I kind of knew him at the start, I knew him really well by the end because we talked about everything.

"I remember asking him about the whole sandpaper incident once, too, He was still working his way through it at the time, trying to figure out how he's dealing with this.

"In his mind I assume he was thinking, 'I'll play 50 more games, become a legend and then I'll earn the respect back of the people'. Unfortunately it didn't work out that way for him and I think that's the thing that's really played on his mind throughout this time.

"I've kept in contact with him periodically. I remember being sat on the bus with him maybe four years ago and I brought this topic up again, asking why he didn't come out and talk about this. He said 'I can't'. He said it to me a few weeks ago actually."

'Bancroft a different person since Sandpapergate revelations

Khawaja continued of Bancroft: "He got in touch with me because he was really struggling. I talked to him on the phone for an hour and a half and told him what I was planning to write in my book.

"That was about halfway during that conversation. The second half of that conversation, I could feel his energy change, because the weight and burden of trying to carry this was eating him up. In his mind, he was thinking, 'no, I'm not the only one here'.

"The first day it came out, he sent me a text saying, 'Uzzy, all I want to say is you've done the right thing and I appreciate this more than you can ever imagine'. That that was one of the things that kept me going because everyone was nailing me that first day.

"We do have a good relationship and a good rapport. He is one of the guys throughout the last two weeks who has been grateful and I needed that, I'm going to be honest, because at times I was like, 'have I done the right thing? Why am I doing this?'

"He finally got to put out a statement. I talked to him afterwards and he's chill, he's laughing, he's joking like he hasn't joked with me in eight years. I can tell that he's a different person.

"If that's the silver lining, it makes it worth it. I can never quite fathom what he went through in those eight years."

articles.title: The England opening batting pair made in Wales
articles.summary: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt became the first Welsh duo to open the batting for England and immediately made cricket headlines.
articles.body:
Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt were made in Wales but have made headlines around the world as England's explosive openers.

The batting pair launched a brutal stand of 151 to guide England to an eight-wicket T20 victory against Australia on the Gold Coast with nearly seven overs left.

Donald blazed 85 in just 32 balls, including striking nine sixes into the stands at the Carrara Oval, with Salt adding another four maximums as he lashed 58 in 30 deliveries.

The pair were born four months apart at opposite ends of Wales in 1996. They have now created history by becoming the first Wales-born pair to open the batting for England.

Seventeen men and five women England cricketers have been born in Wales but there has never been a duo opening the batting before.

"It was pretty special doing that with Salty, two proud Welshmen ticking the box for the England and Wales Cricket Board," said Donald.

"We'll mention it a lot more now. It's a pretty unique position. There's not many sports where you play as two nations together."

Meet Aneurin Donald - the Welshman seizing England chance in Australia

'The rest of the world noticed' - Welshman Donald demolishes Aussies

Salt's path home from Barbados to Welsh Fire captain

Wales do not have a professional cricket side with Glamorgan representing the country as one one of 18 first-class counties alongside 17 English teams.

Former Glamorgan and England spinner Robert Croft, a fluent Welsh speaker and proud Welshman, used to use the analogy when asked about representing England.

"Playing for Glamorgan is like representing Wales, playing for England is like playing for the British and Irish Lions," he said.

Donald started his county career with Glamorgan before moving onto Hampshire and now Derbyshire, while Salt has never played for the Welsh county after joining Lancashire.

Salt, 30, is the more experienced international cricketer having made his international debut in 2021.

He was born to a Welsh mother in Bodelwyddan in north Wales and grew up in St Asaph before moving away to Barbados aged 11 because of his dad's job.

Donald, 29, was born and brought up in the Swansea suburb Gorseinon and was playing only his fifth one-day international after making his England debut in September.

"We are from north and south Wales so have got most basis covered," said Donald.

"Wales probably hasn't produced the guys they'd have liked to after having some good youngsters over the years.

"It's special and it's testament to the system back home.

"Welsh cricket and the support I've had in my career has been incredible and it feels like this is a night where I can give back a little bit."

It was a breakthrough innings for Donald on the international stage as he looks to cement himself on the T20 arena.

Afterwards he was very modest about his cricketing talents with a degree of self-deprecation.

"In the last few years I've realised I'm not great at batting but I'm quite good at slogging," he said.

"In modern cricket I'm not sure there's too much (of a difference), especially in T20, but there might be a career in it now."

Donald says it was about "staying true to himself and trusting his bat swing".

"I'm sure I'm going to make myself look like an idiot over the next few years batting the way I do, but hopefully it's going to come off more often than not," said Donald.

"I'm not the most skilful, I'm not the most powerful but my intent and the way I play has probably separated me out in the last few months.

"There's going to be periods where it's not quite firing but it's about staying as true as I can."

Donald has had to show resilience after recovering from two serious knee injuries.

"It is why you spend all your days either recovering from injury or going through bad form," said Donald.

"It was a nice night to show what I can do and take the next step up.

"I feel like I am in a good place now with T20 cricket and it's a feather in my cap I could show it on a big stage."

It was a moment Donald was able to celebrate with parents Andrew and Jocelyn and uncle Paul who travelled to Australia to watch the five-match series.

The television cameras caught the emotional moments afterwards of Donald hugging his parents.

"My dad was a blubbering mess on the way down to see me at the front, but my mother was more composed," he said.

"It's a a special trip for them and a trip of a lifetime for me so far."

He says he is glad he could reward his family after their long trip but also the important people who had not been able to fly to Australia.

"They are glad they have made the flight out and it is the first time they have been in Australia," said Donald.

"I am glad I can do this in front of them and I am sure we will remember this day for a long time.

"My missus [Heather] and brother [Gafyn] are back home and I am sure they feel they have missed out a bit but they are also so important to me."

Could Donald one day join Salt in the IPL?

So what next for Donald? Former England captain Michael Vaughan has advised him to stick to T20 cricket and predicted he will become a rich man by playing in franchise leagues across the world.

Donald will stay in Australia after the series because he has picked up a contract with Perth Scorchers in the Big Bash league. He will then join Joburg Super Kings in the Betway SA20 in South Africa, which starts in late January.

The Indian Premier League (IPL) remains the mecca for the world's top players.

Salt made his debut in 2023 in the tournament and has been part of three winning sides between 2024 and 2026.

Speaking before flying to Australia, Donald said: "It's still a premium one and it always will be, not just for the financial element, but for the fanfare.

"You've got a billion fans out there. The biggest games, the biggest pressure with the biggest players and those Indian guys are absolute rock stars.

"It would be an incredible experience if I ever did get a crack out there."

Whether there is enough time for Donald to make the 2027 tournament remains to be seen.

He is not on the initial 1,200 long list players for the auction that takes place on 16 December.

That long list is made up of 939 Indians and 281 overseas players, and they will compete for a maximum of 66 places across the 10 teams.

Only 25 of those places are open to overseas players, so competition among the foreign names will be fierce.

Donald still has a limited time to attract the attention of one of the sides who will have witnessed his talents this week.

Whatever happens, Donald will have a taste of India next month. The Perth Scorchers will play against Melbourne Renegades on 12 December in Chennai, which will be the first foreign league to play a regular season fixture in India.

His opening partner that day is likely to be Mitch Marsh, who watched on as Australia's one-day captain on the Gold Coast.

articles.title: South Africa thrash Bangladesh to seal 2-0 sweep before England Test series as Wiaan Mulder takes seven-wicket haul
articles.summary: South Africa host England in a three-Test series live on Sky Sports from December 17, with matches at Johannesburg, Centurion and Cape Town; Proteas hammer Bangladesh inside three days at SuperSport Park to consolidate top spot in World Test Championship
articles.body:
Mulder's knock of 100 from 178 balls came in the hosts' 494-7 declared at Centurion, before the tourists were rolled for 184 in their second dig, having been blown away for 91 on day one of the game when Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen shared six wickets.

South Africa, who face England at home in Tests for the first time since 2020 when the opening game takes place in Johannesburg from December 17, consolidated their position at the top of the World Test Championship as they target back-to-back titles.

The Proteas beat Australia in the Lord's final in 2025, the same side they recently defeated 2-1 in a three-match assignment on home turf after rallying from 1-0 down.

South Africa then saw off Bangladesh by nine wickets in the opening Test at Wanderers, a game in which Mulder was out for a two-ball duck in his sole hit, before this drubbing at SuperSport Park ended when Mulder caught Tigers tailender Khaled Ahmed off Jansen.

Bangladesh battled to 58-0 in their second innings, only to lose two wickets for no runs and three for 20 once Tanzid Hasan (29) edged Mulder behind on the cut, with Mominul Haque (0) glancing the same bowler down the leg-side two overs later.

Once Rabada reduced the visitors to 158-5 by having top-scorer Towhid Hridoy (41) clip meekly to gully, Mulder shredded the middle and lower order.

The all-rounder bowled four other players, including Jaker Ali (2) and Shoriful Islam (0) from successive deliveries, and forced captain Najmul Hossain Shanto (34) to nick off as he found lavish swing movement while bagging a maiden Test five-for.

Mulder said: "I got the ball to go with the wind, ​into the right hander, away from the left hander, and I ​kind of just stuck with that. I tried to target top it off stump ​as often as I could.

"With a little bit of extra movement, I ⁠think I got them playing at balls that they shouldn't, and they created a gap in there to hit the stumps."

Shanto added: "We knew that conditions are tough. Our batters couldn't adapt, especially in the first innings."

articles.title: No ball bowled, batter gone! Deandra Dottin's cizarre WBBL dismissal stuns cricket fans | Watch
articles.summary: Cricket witnessed an unusual dismissal in the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) as West Indies all-rounder Deandra Dottin was sent back to the pavilion
articles.body: Cricket witnessed an unusual dismissal in the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) as West Indies all-rounder Deandra Dottin was sent back to the pavilion without facing a single delivery during Melbourne Renegades' clash against Brisbane Heat.The bizarre incident took place when England spinner Sarah Glenn dismissed Dottin by hitting the stumps after the incoming batter failed to arrive at the crease within the stipulated time. Glenn was given an opportunity to bowl at the unguarded stumps, and she made no mistake.The dismissal came under a special provision in the WBBL playing conditions, which penalises batters who take longer than the permitted time to get ready after a wicket falls.How did Sarah Glenn dismiss Deandra Dottin?Dottin was expected to walk out to bat following the dismissal of Georgia Wareham during Melbourne Renegades' run chase. However, the West Indies all-rounder failed to arrive at the crease within the 75-second time limit. As a result, she was required to stand at least five metres away from the pitch on the leg side for the first delivery.Glenn capitalised on the opportunity and aimed directly at the stumps. The England spinner successfully hit the wicket, leaving Dottin dismissed without facing a ball.What is the 75-second rule in WBBL?The unusual dismissal was made possible by a provision in the WBBL playing conditions designed to prevent unnecessary delays between wickets. Under the rule, an incoming batter must be ready to face the next delivery within 75 seconds of a dismissal or retirement.If the batter fails to meet the deadline, they must remain at least five metres away from the pitch on the leg side, allowing the bowler an opportunity to aim at the unguarded stumps. If the bowler successfully hits the stumps, the incoming batter is dismissed bowled. If the attempt misses, it is recorded as a dot ball.The provision was introduced in the Big Bash competitions during the 2021-22 season to improve the pace of play.Melbourne Renegades clinch thrilling victoryDespite Dottin's unusual dismissal, Melbourne Renegades managed to complete the chase against Brisbane Heat. articles.title: Wiaan Mulder creates Test history, becomes first player to score triple ton and take seven-wicket haul
articles.summary: South Africa all-rounder Wiaan Mulder added another remarkable chapter to his Test career, achieving a rare double that had never been accomplished in the
articles.body: South Africa all-rounder Wiaan Mulder added another remarkable chapter to his Test career, achieving a rare double that had never been accomplished in the history of the longest format. The 28-year-old became the first player to score a triple century and claim a seven-wicket haul during his Test career, producing the historic feat in the second Test against Bangladesh at Centurion.Mulder's exceptional performance with the ball helped South Africa secure a commanding victory by an innings and 219 runs, completing a 2-0 series whitewash against Bangladesh.The achievement brought together two outstanding performances from the all-rounder, who had previously smashed an unbeaten 367 against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo in July 2025 before delivering a career-best bowling display against Bangladesh.From historic triple century to seven-wicket haulMulder had scripted history during the second Test against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo on July 7, 2025, when he scored an unbeaten 367 on his Test captaincy debut. He reached the triple-century mark in just 297 deliveries, producing one of the finest innings by a South African batter in Test cricket. The Proteas eventually registered an innings-and-236-run victory.Nearly a year later, Mulder added another historic achievement to his name, this time with the ball against Bangladesh.The all-rounder returned sensational figures of 7/31 in the second innings, helping South Africa bowl out Bangladesh and seal a comprehensive victory.Mulder registers South Africa's best bowling figures against BangladeshMulder's 7/31 became the best bowling figures by a South African in a Test innings against Bangladesh. He surpassed Keshav Maharaj's previous record of 7/32, recorded in Durban in 2022. Maharaj had also claimed 7/40 in Gqeberha during the same year.Mulder's performance was also the second-best bowling return in a Test innings at Centurion. Kyle Abbott continues to hold the venue record with figures of 7/29 against Pakistan in 2013.Joins elite list of players with century and seven-wicket haulThe exclusive list features some of the greatest all-rounders in cricket history, including:Jack Gregory (Australia) against England in Melbourne, 1920.Ian Botham (England) against Pakistan at Lord's, 1978.Ian Botham (England) against India at Mumbai, 1980.Ravichandran Ashwin (India) against West Indies at North Sound, 2016.Naseer Khan Maroofkhil (Afghanistan) against Zimbabwe in Sharjah, 2026.Wiaan Mulder (South Africa) against Bangladesh at Centurion.Sets another record with fastest seven-wicket haulMulder's remarkable bowling performance also saw him establish a new record for the fastest seven-wicket haul by a fourth-change bowler or later in a Test innings. The South African all-rounder needed just 64 deliveries to claim his seven wickets, surpassing the previous record held by Hugh Tayfield.Tayfield had taken 68 balls to register a seven-wicket haul against Australia in Durban in 1950.South Africa complete 2-0 series whitewashMulder's individual brilliance was complemented by an impressive team performance as South Africa dominated Bangladesh in the second Test. Marques Ackermann played a crucial role with the bat, scoring 150, while the Proteas' bowling attack kept Bangladesh under pressure throughout the contest.Marco Jansen also contributed with three wickets across Bangladesh's innings as the hosts secured an innings-and-219-run victory to complete a 2-0 series whitewash.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
